structure.proved_step: LEMMA (sharpened expectation and deterministic poly-time restriction). Setting: n>=2, 1<=k<n, r=n-k, m>=1, W in {+-1}^{m x n}, t in Z^m, F subset [n] with |F|=k, G=[n]\F. For z in {0,1}^G define N_F(z) = #{j : the gate y -> [W_j.(z,y) >= t_j] is non-constant in y in {0,1}^F}. Claim: (a) E_{z uniform} N_F(z) <= m k beta_r, with beta_r = C(r, floor(r/2))/2^r; (b) beta_r <= 1/sqrt(r); (c) there is a deterministic procedure, polynomial in n and m, that outputs z with N_F(z) <= E_z N_F <= m k/sqrt(r). PROOF. Fix gate j, put A_j(z) = sum_{i in G} W_ji z_i and S_j(y) = sum_{i in F} W_ji y_i. The gate is non-constant iff some y has A_j+S_j >= t_j and some y' has A_j+S_j < t_j, i.e. iff t_j - maxS_j <= A_j < t_j - minS_j. Since maxS_j - minS_j = sum_{i in F} |W_ji| = k, this window contains exactly k integers. Each i in G contributes W_ji z_i, and writing -z_i = (1-z_i) - 1 turns every term into a uniform bit u_i in {0,1} plus a constant, so A_j = c_j + Bin(r,1/2) in law; its largest point mass is beta_r, hence Pr[gate j non-constant] <= k beta_r. Linearity gives (a). For (b): with a = floor(r/2), C(2a,a)/4^a <= 1/sqrt(pi a) and r=2a gives beta_r <= 1/sqrt(pi r/2) <= 1/sqrt(r); for r=2a+1, beta_r = C(2a,a)/4^a * (2a+1)/(2a+2) <= 1/sqrt(pi a) <= 1/sqrt(2a+1) when a>=1, and beta_1 = 1/2 <= 1. For (c), conditional expectations: for a prefix of bits of z, E[N | prefix] = sum_j Pr[gate j non-constant | prefix]; each term is the mass of a window of k integers under a sum of the remaining independent uniform bits plus a known constant, computable exactly by an O(r^2) DP per gate. Choose the next bit as the value with smaller conditional expectation. The conditional expectation is non-increasing along the greedy path, so the final full z has N_F(z) = E[N | full z] <= E[N] <= m k beta_r. Total cost O(r * m * r^2) arithmetic operations. SCOPE: +-1 weights, arbitrary integer thresholds, any fixed F. This is the restriction step of lane G with the worst-case-over-z replaced by a per-instance minimum that the greedy procedure finds in polynomial time. It does NOT bound the worst case over z: for W with identical rows all equal to (1,...,1), t_j = 1, k = 1, F = {1}, the assignment z = 0 makes all m gates non-constant, so max_z N_F(z) = m > m/sqrt(n-1) for every n >= 3 (identical-rows counterexample, to be checked by exact enumeration).

structure.proved_step: LEMMA (shared-weight MAJ o MAJ counting). Let w in Z^n with |w_i| <= W, thresholds t_1..t_m in Z, weights v_j in Z, integer T, and C(x) = [sum_j v_j [w.x >= t_j] >= T] for x in {0,1}^n. Then #{x : C(x)=1} is computed exactly in O(n^2 W + m) arithmetic operations. Proof: s(x) = w.x ranges over an integer interval R of size at most 2nW+1. The DP dist_0 = {0:1}, dist_i = dist_{i-1} convolved with {0:1, w_i:1} gives dist_n(s) = #{x : w.x = s} exactly, in O(n * |R|) time. Since C depends on x only through s, the answer is sum over s in R with g(s) >= T of dist_n(s), where g(s) = sum_j v_j [s >= t_j] is computed for all s in R by sorting thresholds and prefix sums in O(|R| + m). Correctness follows since the DP counts x by their value of w.x. Scope: one shared weight vector, bounded integer weights. This is a restricted subclass only: it does not decide the general MAJ o MAJ CAPP obligation (G0001) and does not handle distinct bottom weight vectors.

structure.proved_step: LEMMA (k-class DP for MAJ o MAJ, exact). Let W >= 1, k >= 1, n >= 1. Let w^(1),...,w^(k) in Z^n with |w^(c)_i| <= W. Let bottom gates g_j(x) = [w^(c_j).x >= t_j] for j = 1..m with class labels c_j in {1..k}, integer thresholds t_j, integer top weights v_j, and integer T. Let C(x) = [sum_j v_j g_j(x) >= T]. Then #{x in {0,1}^n : C(x) = 1} is computed exactly in time O(n k S + m S) where S <= min(2^n, (nW+1)^k) is the number of distinct states. Proof: (i) u(x) = (w^(1).x, ..., w^(k).x) in Z^k; C depends on x only through u(x), since g_j depends only on u_{c_j}(x). (ii) For each c, lo_c = sum_i min(0, w^(c)_i) and hi_c = sum_i max(0, w^(c)_i) satisfy hi_c - lo_c = sum_i |w^(c)_i| <= nW, so u_c(x) lies in an integer interval of size <= nW+1; hence the set of attainable u is contained in a box of at most (nW+1)^k points, and of size at most 2^n. (iii) The DP dist_0 = {0^k: 1}, dist_i(u) = dist_{i-1}(u) + dist_{i-1}(u - col_i), where col_i = (w^(1)_i,...,w^(k)_i), satisfies dist_n(u) = #{x : u(x) = u}; each layer has at most S states. (iv) The answer is the sum of dist_n(u) over u with sum_j v_j [u_{c_j} >= t_j] >= T. Consequence: for k <= (1-delta) n / log2(n W + 1) the count is computed exactly in time 2^{(1-delta) n} poly(n) (since (nW+1)^k <= 2^{(1-delta) n}). For W = 1: k <= (1-delta) n / log2(n+1) gives 2^{(1-delta) n} poly(n), with exact output, so the error is 0 and the algorithm is deterministic. Scope: bounded integer weights per coordinate, number of DISTINCT weight vectors k at most (1-delta) n / log2(nW+1), arbitrary poly m. This is a restricted subclass. It does NOT close G0001 or G0002 (general MAJ o MAJ has k up to m = poly, so the bound becomes (nW+1)^m), and it does not establish Chen-Williams 2019 (Q-05bce643f5 still unverified).

structure.proved_step: LEMMA (claimed, for review). Setup: W_j in {-1,+1}^n, F subset [n] with |F|=k, R=[n]\F, f=n-k, M_j = #{i in R: W_ji=-1}, delta in (0,1/2). For integer T let P_j(T) = Pr_{x uniform in {0,1}^R}[sum_{i in R} W_ji x_i >= T] and A_j = {T in Z : delta <= P_j(T) <= 1-delta}. For z in {0,1}^F let T_j(z) = t_j - sum_{i in F} W_ji z_i, and flip_j(z,z') = [T_j(z) in A_j] xor [T_j(z') in A_j]. (a) A_j is an integer interval (possibly empty). Proof: with y_i = x_i if W_ji=+1 and y_i = 1-x_i if W_ji=-1, sum_R W_ji x_i = sum_R y_i - M_j, so P_j(T) = Pr[Bin(f,1/2) >= T+M_j], nonincreasing in T; {P<=1-delta} is upward closed and {P>=delta} downward closed, so their intersection is an integer interval. (b) If flip_j(z,z') then dist(T_j(z), {min A_j, max A_j}) <= |Delta_j|, Delta_j = T_j(z') - T_j(z). Proof: write T=T_j(z), T'=T+Delta, A=[L,H]. If T in A and T' not in A then T' < L or T' > H, so T is within |Delta| of L or of H (T-L < L-... i.e. T' < L gives T-L < -Delta <= |Delta|, and T'>H gives H-T < Delta). Symmetric for T not in A, T' in A. (c) Let the thresholds t_j be independent of (z,z') with Pr[t_j = v] <= rho for all v in Z. Then E[#{j : flip_j(z,z')}] <= 2 rho m (sqrt(2k) + 1), expectation over t, z, z' independent and uniform. Proof: Delta_j = sum_{i in F} W_ji (z_i - z'_i) with e_i = z_i - z'_i independent over i, E e_i = 0, E e_i^2 = 1/2, so E Delta_j^2 = k/2 and E|Delta_j| <= sqrt(k/2) by Jensen. Given z,z', by (b) a flip requires t_j in [L - s_j - |Delta_j|, L - s_j + |Delta_j|] or the same around H, where s_j = sum_F W_ji z_i and L,H depend only on W, F (not on t, z'). Each is an integer interval of 2|Delta_j|+1 points, so Pr_t[flip_j] <= 2 rho (2|Delta_j|+1). Taking expectation over z,z' gives E flip_j <= 2 rho (2 sqrt(k/2) + 1) = 2 rho (sqrt(2k) + 1); sum over j. (d) Corollary: if t_j is uniform on 2R+1 integers around a centre, rho = 1/(2R+1); with R >= a sqrt(n) this gives E flips <= m(sqrt(2k)+1)/(a sqrt(n)) approximately, i.e. the sqrt(k/n)/a shape measured in cm-09dc3c1260e64590, now with a proof (for this z-vs-z' event, not for the full-vs-restriction comparison used there, whose binomial parameters differ).

structure.lemma: Suffix-separation lemma (deterministic, conditional on a collision). For every n≥1 and distinct u,v∈{0,1}^n, define y=u∧¬v if u∧¬v≠0, and otherwise y=v∧¬u. Then exactly one of u,v is disjoint from y. Consequently, for any deterministic one-pass streaming algorithm A whose states after u and v are equal, A gives the same answer on (u,y) and (v,y), although their DISJ answers differ, so A errs on at least one of these two inputs. Proof: In the first case, y has a 1 only where u has a 1 and v has a 0; hence u intersects y and v is disjoint from y. In the second case u∧¬v=0, so every 1 of u is also a 1 of v. Since u≠v, v∧¬u≠0; y is then disjoint from u and intersects v. Equal streaming states after the prefixes, followed by the same suffix, yield equal final states and outputs. This proves only suffix construction once a collision is supplied; it does not uniformly select a colliding pair or address randomized algorithms.

structure.proved_step: CLAIMED, kind ALGORITHM (boundary result, does NOT close G0001). Statement: let W in Z^{m x n}, t, v in Z^m, T in Z, and suppose the supports S_1..S_m of the rows of W are pairwise disjoint, |S_j| = k_j. Let c_j = #{y in {0,1}^{S_j} : sum_{i in S_j} W[j,i] y_i >= t_j}. Then #{x in {0,1}^n : sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T} = 2^f * sum_{e >= T} [z^e] prod_j ((2^{k_j} - c_j) + c_j z^{v_j}), with f = n - sum_j k_j. Proof: under uniform x, the events E_j = [W_j.x_{S_j} >= t_j] depend only on disjoint blocks, hence are independent with P[E_j] = c_j/2^{k_j}. Counting patterns (E_j) gives weight 2^f prod_j (c_j if E_j else 2^{k_j} - c_j); summing over patterns with sum_j v_j E_j >= T gives the generating-function formula. Running time: O(sum_j 2^{k_j}) to compute the c_j, plus m block updates on a polynomial of at most m*V+1 coefficients (V = max |v_j|). Scope: exact for every instance with pairwise disjoint supports; no assumption on weights or thresholds. Evidence: cm-07270f02ad1441eb (60 random disjoint-block instances, n in {8,10,12}, 0 mismatches vs brute force, EXPLORATORY_COMPUTATION). Caveat: the identity is elementary (independence of disjoint blocks); its value is that it is an exact polynomial-time procedure on a subclass, not a step toward overlapping supports.

structure.proved_step: CLAIMED, kind ALGORITHM (addresses G0001; closure not claimed, pending independent review). Setting: f(x) = [sum_j v_j [sum_{i in S_j} w_{ji} x_i >= t_j] >= T] over x in {0,1}^n, with |S_j| <= k, each variable in at most D supports S_j, m gates, V = max |v_j|. Claim: #f can be computed exactly in time poly(n, m, V) * 2^{n - n/(Dk+1)}. Proof: fix an order of variables; let A_p be the set of variables at positions <= p that lie in some S_j containing a variable at a position > p. Each gate touching A_p contains a suffix variable, so |A_p| <= min(p, Dk(n-p)), and max_p min(p, a(n-p)) = n - n/(a+1) for a = Dk. Dynamic program over p: state = assignment to A_p, value = polynomial in z whose exponent is the sum of v_j over gates already decided. A gate with last position p is determined by the state at step p, since its earlier variables lie in A_{p-1}. Exactness is by induction on p. Time: sum_p 2^{|A_p|} * (2mV+1) * m * 2^k. Scope: all instances with fan-in <= k and max variable degree <= D; weights and thresholds arbitrary. Consequence: for m = n^alpha, alpha < 2, fixed k, D = C n^{alpha-1}, the saving is 2^{Omega(n^{2-alpha})}, superpolynomial, so 2^n / n^{omega(1)} for that subclass. Evidence: cm-7f058b7dae1d4e23 (60 random instances, n in {8,10,12,14}, k in {2,3}; 0 brute mismatches, 0 frontier-bound violations). The exponent itself is not measured; it is a bound.

structure.proved_step: CLAIMED, kind ALGORITHM (sub-case, does NOT close G0001). Statement: let f(x) = [sum_j v_j [W_j . x >= t_j] >= T] on {0,1}^n with integer W, t, v, T and m rows, and let U = union of supp(W_j) over all j with |U| = s. Then #{x in {0,1}^n : f(x)=1} = 2^(n-s) * #{y in {0,1}^U : f(y)=1}, and the right-hand count is computed in time O(2^s * m * s) by enumerating y in {0,1}^U and evaluating each gate. Proof: for each j, W_j . x = W_j|_U . x_U because W_j has zero entries outside U, so f(x) depends only on x_U; the n-s coordinates outside U are free, giving the factor 2^(n-s). The enumeration evaluates m gates of support <= s at each of the 2^s points. Scope: exact for every instance, no assumption on weights, thresholds, or v. Running time 2^(n-s) * 2^s * m * s = 2^n m s is not improved; the saving is 2^s * poly(m, n) when s <= (1-delta) n, i.e. 2^{(1-delta) n} poly. Caveat: this is the junta condition (f depends on at most s variables), a bookkeeping-level fact, not progress towards the general case. For the target size m = n^1.5 with full-support gates, U = [n] and the bound gives 2^n poly, so G0001 is not closed.

structure.proved_step: LEMMA-DIR (repair of S0002 for G0001). Setting: n >= 1, B >= 1, D >= 1. Directions a_1..a_D in Z^n with |a_{d,i}| <= B. Gates j = 1..m, each with direction d(j), threshold t_j in Z, weight v_j in Z. Threshold T in Z. Let N(F) = #{x in {0,1}^n : sum_j v_j [a_{d(j)} . x >= t_j] >= T}. CLAIM: N(F) is computed exactly in O(n (2Bn+1)^D (D+m)) arithmetic operations on integers of O(n + log(m B)) bits. PROOF: Let Y(x) = (a_1.x, ..., a_D.x) in Z^D and N_y = #{x : Y(x) = y}. Then N(F) = sum over y of N_y [g(y) >= T], where g(y) = sum_j v_j [y_{d(j)} >= t_j]. Let N^(i)_y count the prefixes x_1..x_i with partial sums y. Recursion: N^(i)_y = N^(i-1)_y + N^(i-1)_{y - c_i}, where c_i = (a_{1,i}, ..., a_{D,i}), because x_i in {0,1}. N^(0) is the point mass at 0. The support of N^(i) lies in the box [-iB, iB]^D, which has at most (2iB+1)^D <= (2Bn+1)^D points. Each step costs at most (2Bn+1)^D D operations. Evaluating g at each of these points costs O(m) naively. The total is therefore O(n (2Bn+1)^D (D+m)). COROLLARY (the subclass): if D <= (1-delta) n / log2(2Bn+1), then (2Bn+1)^D <= 2^{(1-delta) n}, so the running time is 2^{(1-delta) n} times n^{O(1)}, and this holds for every m = poly(n), including m = n^alpha for any alpha > 1. For B = poly(n), the condition reads D <= (1-delta') n / log n. The subclass is defined by few distinct weight vectors, not by disjoint supports, so it allows overlapping supports and m > n. SCOPE: the subclass only. It does not cover D = Theta(n) distinct directions, and it is not a general #SAT algorithm.

structure.proved_step: LEMMA-ARR (CLAIMED, scope: m bottom gates, any n). For integer W in Z^{m x n}, t in Z^m, the number of distinct patterns P(x) = ([W_j.x >= t_j])_j over x in {0,1}^n is at most sum_{i=0}^{n} C(m,i) <= (e m / n)^n. Proof: [W_j.x >= t_j] iff W_j.x > t_j - 1/2 for integer x, so P(x) is the sign vector of x with respect to the m affine hyperplanes H_j = {y : W_j.y = t_j - 1/2} in R^n. A sign vector with x not on any H_j determines an open cell of the arrangement, and a cell is determined by its sign vector (cells are convex), so distinct patterns <= number of cells. Buck (1943) / Cover (1965): an arrangement of m hyperplanes in R^n has at most sum_{i<=n} C(m,i) regions. Consequence: for m <= n/4, patterns <= (e/4)^n <= 2^{0.56 n}, i.e. delta = 0.44. Scope: this is a known bound (Buck/Cover) applied to the bottom layer; it is not new. It does NOT close G0001: for m = n^alpha with alpha > 1 the bound is at least 2^n, and no algorithm enumerating the realised patterns in 2^{(1-delta)n} time is given.

structure.proved_step: ALG-FEWDIR (CLAIMED, scope: THR o THR circuits C(x) = [sum_j v_j [<W_j,x> >= t_j] >= T] over x in {0,1}^n, where all bottom weight vectors W_j in Z^n take at most D distinct values d_1..d_D, and |entries| <= B. Claim: #C = #{x : C(x)=1} is computed exactly in O(n * m * D * (2nB+1)^D) arithmetic operations. Proof: (i) For x, let s(x) = (<d_1,x>,...,<d_D,x>) in Z^D. Every bottom gate equals [s_{g(j)}(x) >= t_j] for its direction index g(j), so C(x) is a function F(s(x)) with F(s) = [sum_j v_j [s_{g(j)} >= t_j] >= T]. (ii) Dynamic programming: after processing variables x_1..x_i, let N_i(s) = #{(x_1..x_i) : s(x_1..x_i)=s}. Then N_0 = {0:1} and N_{i} is obtained from N_{i-1} by adding 0 or d_{1,i},...,d_{D,i} to each state, which is exact by induction. (iii) #C = sum_{s} N_n(s) F(s). (iv) Each coordinate of s(x) lies in [-nB, nB], so at most (2nB+1)^D states exist at every step. Each step does at most 2 * (2nB+1)^D updates of O(D) work, and evaluating F on a state costs O(m). Total O(n (2nB+1)^D (D + m)). Consequence: for D <= c log n and B <= n^k, the time is 2^{O(log^2 n)} * poly(n), hence 2^n / n^{omega(1)} for this subclass. Scope: a subclass of THR o THR where the number of distinct bottom directions is O(log n). This is a proof for the subclass only. For general m = n^alpha the number of distinct directions can be m, and the bound becomes 2^{Omega(n^{c})}. It does NOT close G0001 or G0007. The result is a standard counting argument, not new; its use is as an O2 subclass theorem.

structure.proved_step: PROCEDURE (path-order DP, CLAIMED, unreviewed). Setting: g_j(x)=[sum_{u in S_j} w_{j,u} x_u >= t_j], |S_j|<=k, integer weights, top weights v_j with |v_j|<=V, threshold T, m gates. Fix a linear order pi on [n]; for each position i let A_i = {u <=_pi i : u in S_j for some j with max_pi S_j >_pi i} and w(pi)=max_i |A_i|. Then N = #{x: sum_j v_j g_j(x) >= T} is computed exactly in time O(n 2^{w(pi)} (2mV+1) mk). Proof: DP table D_i indexed by (a in {0,1}^{A_i}, s in [-mV,mV]) with invariant c = #{y in {0,1}^{<=i}: y|_{A_i}=a, sigma_i(y)=s}, where sigma_i(y) = sum over gates with max S_j <= i of v_j g_j(y_{S_j}). Base D_{-1}={(empty,0):1}. Step: a gate with max S_j=i has support inside A_{i-1} union {i} (any u<i in S_j has max S_j > i-1, so u in A_{i-1}), so its contribution depends only on (a', b) with b = y_i; hence D_i is a function of D_{i-1}. At the end A_{n-1} is empty and the answer is sum_{s>=T} D_{n-1}(empty,s). Table size per step is at most 2^w (2mV+1). Qed. Scope: an exact procedure parameterised by w(pi). It is the standard path-decomposition DP, so a reviewer may judge it trivial. It does NOT close G0002, because G0002 also needs pw <= (1-delta) n for a stated subclass of size n^alpha, which is not proved. Full-support gates force w = n-1 under the identity order.

structure.lemma: BOUNDARY DP (repair of G0002, construction half only). Fix a THR o THR circuit f(x) = [sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T] on n variables, and an ordering pi of the variables. For a prefix P_k = {pi_1..pi_k} let B_k = the placed variables that lie in some bottom gate whose support is not inside P_k. Claim: #{x : f(x)=1} is computed exactly by a DP over the states (a|B_k, s_k), where a|B_k is the assignment to B_k and s_k = sum over bottom gates completed by P_k of v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] (an integer in [-V, V], V = sum |v_j|). Proof: for any completion y of the unplaced variables, the still-open gates j have W_j.x = W_j.(a|B_k, y) + const, so their values depend only on a|B_k; completed gates contribute only through s_k. Two prefixes with equal (a|B_k, s_k) therefore have identical completion counts, which justifies the merge. Hence the count is exact and the running time is n * max_k 2^{|B_k|} * (2V+1) * poly(m). Scope: a bound on time for a class needs a bound on max_k |B_k| for ALL instances in the class.

structure.lemma: Clipped-State DP for THR∘THR #SAT. Let C be a THR∘THR circuit on n variables with m = n^α bottom gates (α > 0). Split variables into X_A (first a = ⌊n/2⌋) and X_B (rest). For each bottom gate j, let W^A_j, W^B_j be its weights on X_A, X_B; threshold t_j. Define lo_j = min_{x_B} W^B_j·x_B, hi_j = max_{x_B} W^B_j·x_B. For x_A ∈ {0,1}^a, the clipped vector c(x_A) ∈ ℤ^m has entries c_j = clip(t_j - W^A_j·x_A, lo_j, hi_j + 1). Then #SAT(C) = Σ_{c ∈ C} |{x_A : c(x_A) = c}| · R(c), where R(c) = |{x_B : (W^B_j·x_B ≥ c_j for all j) is satisfied and the top threshold holds}|. The number of distinct clip vectors K_clip ≤ Π_j (|{W^B_j·x_B : x_B ∈ {0,1}^b}| + 2).
structure.proved_step: Lemma statement recorded. Next: prove the exactness (counting identity) and bound K_clip. The identity holds because for fixed x_A, the condition W_j·x ≥ t_j is equivalent to W^B_j·x_B ≥ t_j - W^A_j·x_A. Since W^B_j·x_B ∈ [lo_j, hi_j], values below lo_j are always true (so clip to lo_j), values above hi_j are always false (so clip to hi_j+1 as an impossible threshold). Thus the condition depends on x_A only through c(x_A). Summing over c gives the exact count. The bound on K_clip follows because each c_j takes at most |supp_B(j)| + 2 values.

structure.lemma: SUBCLASS DP (exact, proved). Let C = THR o THR with n Boolean inputs, m bottom gates [W_j.x >= t_j], integer weights 0 <= W_j,i <= B, top weights v_j and threshold T. Suppose the m weight vectors take at most c distinct values (as vectors, indexed by inv(j)). Then #{x : C(x)=1} is computed by the layered DP over states s in [0, Bn]^c (s_d = W_d . x_{<i} after i variables) in time O(n * m * min(2^n, (Bn+1)^c)) arithmetic operations. Proof: after reading x_0..x_{i-1} define s(x_{<i}) in [0,Bn]^c. Each bottom gate value [W_j.x >= t_j] is a function of s_{inv(j)} at the end, and the step x_i -> s + b*W_{.,i} is a deterministic map on states. So the map x -> s(x) is a function from {0,1}^n to states that commutes with each step; the count of x with s(x)=s equals the DP count (induction on i). C(x) depends only on s(x) at i=n, so #C = sum over final states s satisfying the top predicate of the DP count. Each layer has at most min(2^i, (Bn+1)^c) states.
structure.proved_step: CLAIMED: For c <= n / (2 log2(Bn+1)), the DP runs in 2^{n/2} * poly(n, m) time, a saving of 2^{n/2}, which is larger than n^{omega(1)} for the subclass. Proof: (Bn+1)^c = 2^{c log2(Bn+1)} <= 2^{n/2}. Correctness is the induction above. Scope: exact subclass with few distinct weight vectors; it is NOT a general algorithm and the generic families (D = m, measured) fall outside it.

structure.lemma: CUTWIDTH DP (subclass, exact). Let C = THR o THR on n Boolean inputs with m bottom gates [W_j.x >= t_j], integer weights 0 <= W_{j,i} <= B, supports S_j, top weights v_j, threshold T. Fix a variable order 0..n-1 and let a_i = #{j : some variable of S_j lies below i and some lies at or above i} (gates active at cut i). Then #{x : C(x)=1} is computed by a layered DP whose state after reading x_0..x_{i-1} is (number of completed gates whose value is 1, partial sums of the active gates). Partial sums of an active gate lie in [0, B s], so the layer has at most (m+1)(Bs+1)^{a_i} states, and the total work is at most 2n(m+1) max_i (Bs+1)^{a_i}. Correctness: the final value of each gate depends on its partial sum at cut i plus contributions from x_{>=i}, so the state is a sufficient statistic and the DP counts are exact by induction on i. Consequence: if a_i <= (1-delta) n / log2(Bs+1) for all i, #C is computed in 2^{(1-delta) n} poly(n) time. This recovers the box bound for m <= (1-delta)n/log2(Bs+1) as the special case a_i = m.

structure.proved_step: BANDWIDTH WINDOW DP (subclass, exact, O2). Let C(x) = [sum_j v_j [W_j . x >= t_j] >= T] on x in {0,1}^n, with integer W_{j,k} >= 0, integer t_j, integer v_j >= 0, V = sum_j v_j, and S_j = supp(W_j). Bandwidth b: for every bottom gate j, max S_j - min S_j <= b. Let first_j = min S_j and last_j = max S_j. CLAIM: #{x : C(x)=1} is computed exactly with O((V+1) 2^b poly(n,m)) operations. PROOF. Read x_0,...,x_{n-1} in order. After reading x_0..x_{i-1}, the state is (u, sigma): u = sum of v_j over gates with last_j < i and value 1; sigma_j = sum over k in S_j, k < i, of W_{j,k} x_k for each gate with first_j < i <= last_j (active); sigma_j = 0 for gates with first_j >= i. Keep counts N_i(u, sigma) of prefixes. SUFFICIENCY: finished gates are already fixed in u; each active gate's final value is [sigma_j + sum over k in S_j, k >= i of W_{j,k} x_k >= t_j], which depends only on sigma_j and the suffix. So the number of completions with C = 1 depends only on (u, sigma), and the layer-to-layer transition is exact by induction; at i = n, C = [u >= T]. WINDOW: for an active gate, last_j >= i and last_j - first_j <= b give first_j >= i - b, so sigma_j is a function of x_{i-b}..x_{i-1}. Hence sigma takes at most 2^b values and each layer has at most (V+1) 2^b states. CONSEQUENCE: for b <= (1-delta) n the count takes 2^{(1-delta) n} poly(n, m) time (V poly-bounded). NON-VACUITY: for every alpha the class contains circuits of size n^alpha (supports inside windows of length n/2, many distinct gates available), so this is a proved running time for a subclass of size n^alpha. Weights W are not restricted in size; only the number of distinct sigma values matters.

structure.lemma: BANDWIDTH-DP (restated). C = THR o THR on variables 0..n-1 with m bottom gates g_j(x) = [sum_{i in S_j} c_{j,i} x_i >= t_j], supports S_j contained in an interval [a_j, a_j + w - 1] (w = max_j (max S_j - min S_j) + 1), |c_{j,i}| <= B, integer top weights v_j, R = sum_j |v_j|, top threshold T. Then N(C) = #{x : sum_j v_j g_j(x) >= T} is computed exactly in O(2^(w-1) (2R+1) (n + m w)) operations.
structure.proved_step: PROOF. Read x_0, ..., x_{n-1} in order. After reading x_0..x_{k-1} define the window sigma_k = (x_{k-w+1}, ..., x_{k-1}) (indices < 0 read as 0; 2^(w-1) possibilities) and the partial top sum P_k = sum over j with max S_j < k of v_j g_j(x). Each gate with max S_j = k has S_j inside [k-w+1, k], so g_j(x) is a function of (sigma_k, x_k): the transition P_{k+1} = P_k + sum_{j: max S_j = k} v_j g_j(sigma_k, x_k), sigma_{k+1} = last w-1 bits of (sigma_k, x_k) is well defined. Induction on k: the number of completions of a prefix that give top sum >= T depends only on (sigma_k, P_k), since later gates read only the window and later variables. Hence the DP over keys (sigma, P) with counts is exact. |P_k| <= R, so at most 2^(w-1)(2R+1) keys per step, and each step costs O(keys * (2 + m w)). Final answer: sum of counts over keys with P_n >= T. COROLLARY: if w <= (1-delta) n and R <= poly(n), time is 2^((1-delta) n) poly(n, m) on this subclass. Scope: the subclass requires every bottom support to lie in a window of length (1-delta) n under a fixed variable order; generic random supports of size Theta(n) fall outside it.

Then Pr[M_k nonconstant] = sum_{f=1}^{k} P(Bin(k,p)=f) * P(t-f <= Bin(k-f,1/2) <= t-1). Since the window {t-f,...,t-1} has f points and max_j P(Bin(m,1/2)=j) <= sqrt(2/(pi m))(1+o(1)), we get Pr <= E[f] sqrt(2/(pi(k-f))) = sqrt(2/pi) p sqrt(k) (1+o(1)) + tail, where the tail is controlled by Chernoff for f > k/2. structure.proved_step: CLAIMED LEMMA (kind LEMMA; closes only the tail gap G0051(i), not G0007). Setting: k >= 4, S a set of k variables, t = floor((k+1)/2), M(x) = [sum_{i in S} x_i >= t]. A random restriction keeps each variable of S free independently with probability p in [0,1] and fixes the others to uniform bits. Claim: Pr[M|rho nonconstant] <= (2/sqrt(pi)) sqrt(k/(k-2)) p sqrt(k) + (4p)^{k/2}. PROOF. Let F ~ Bin(k,p) be the number of free variables in S. Given F = f, the fixed part has m = k-f variables and sum s ~ Bin(m,1/2). M|rho is nonconstant iff s <= t-1 and s+f >= t, i.e. s in the window [t-f, t-1], which has f integers. So W_f := Pr[nonconstant | F=f] <= f * max_j P(Bin(m,1/2)=j). (a) Max-pmf bound: for m >= 2, max_j P(Bin(m,1/2)=j) <= sqrt(2/(pi(m-1))). Proof: C(2r,r)/4^r <= 1/sqrt(pi r) for r >= 1 (standard). If m = 2r, the max is C(2r,r)/4^r <= sqrt(2/(pi m)) <= sqrt(2/(pi(m-1))). If m = 2r+1, the max is C(2r,r)/4^r * (2r+1)/(2r+2) <= 1/sqrt(pi r) = sqrt(2/(pi(m-1))). (b) Part f <= k/2: then m >= k/2 >= 2 and m-1 >= (k-2)/2, so W_f <= 2f/sqrt(pi(k-2)). Summing with E[F] = kp gives sum_{f<=k/2} P(F=f) W_f <= 2kp/sqrt(pi(k-2)) = (2/sqrt(pi)) sqrt(k/(k-2)) p sqrt(k). (c) Part f > k/2: sum_{f>k/2} P(F=f) W_f <= P(F >= k/2). Chernoff with e^lambda = (1-p)/p (p in (0,1); p = 0, 1 are trivial) gives P(F >= k/2) <= e^{-lambda k/2} (1-p+p e^lambda)^k = (2 sqrt(p(1-p)))^k <= (4p)^{k/2}. Adding (b) and (c) gives the claim. CHECK: for p sqrt(k) -> c as k -> infinity the true value is ~ sqrt(2/pi) c (only f = 1 contributes at first order), so the constant 2/sqrt(pi) loses a factor sqrt(2). The tail (4p)^{k/2} is informative only for p < 1/4. SCOPE: unit-weight majority, every k >= 4, every p in [0,1]. Finite check cm-ead2ddafe1824903 (558 cases, k = 4..59 and 64..1024, p in [1e-4, 0.25]): no violation of either the window bound or the total bound; worst ratio 0.71 (at k = 1024, p = 1e-4). That check corroborates the argument but does not prove it.

structure.lemma: Per-gate restriction lemma (repair of the R0948 step). Let W_j in Z^n with max |W_ji| <= B, threshold t_j in Z, and g_j(x) = [W_j.x >= t_j]. Fix a set F of k variables and draw the other variables uniformly. Let r = |supp(W_j) minus F| >= 1. Then Pr[g_j non-constant | F] <= (sum over i in F of |W_ji|) * C(r, floor(r/2)) / 2^r <= B k / sqrt(r).
structure.proved_step: Proof. (1) Write c = sum over free i with W_ji nonzero of W_ji x_i, and U = W_j restricted to F, lo = sum min(U_i, 0), hi = sum max(U_i, 0). The gate is non-constant iff t_j - hi <= c < t_j - lo, i.e. c lies in a set of L = hi - lo consecutive integers, with L <= sum over F of |W_ji| <= Bk. (2) Erdos (1945, Sperner): for reals a_i with |a_i| >= 1, any open interval of length 2 contains at most C(r, floor(r/2)) of the 2^r subset sums. Apply it to the open interval (s-1, s+1) with s an integer: Pr[c = s] <= C(r, floor(r/2))/2^r. (The earlier version used a window of length 2 with integer weights, which is false: a=(1,1), window (0.5,2.5). The point bound is correct.) (3) Union over the L integer values gives Pr[non-constant | F] <= L C(r, floor(r/2))/2^r. (4) C(r, floor(r/2))/2^r <= 1/sqrt(r) for all r >= 1 (standard central-binomial estimate). Hence the bound. QED. Exact checks: cm-11329b5046ac4967 (old window-2 version: 24 violations, refuted) and cm-0fc2b38402284a21 (point version: 0 violations in 300 instances, worst ratio 1.0).

structure.lemma: LEMMA-R2K (subclass R(k,B): each variable read by at most 2 bottom gates, each bottom gate reads at most k variables, bottom weights |W| <= B, top weights |v| <= V, integer thresholds). Let G be the multigraph on the non-constant bottom gates with one edge per variable read by two gates and one pendant half-edge per variable read by one gate. Let pw be its pathwidth. Then #SAT is computed exactly by a variable-order DP whose state is the tuple of partial sums of open gates plus the top accumulator, in time poly(n,m) * (2Bk+1)^(pw+1) * (2Vm+1). Proof: take a path decomposition of G with width pw and the layout of gates it induces (vertex separation <= pw); process variables ordered by their larger endpoint. A gate is open after a prefix iff it has a processed edge and an unprocessed edge, so at most pw+1 gates are open. An open partial sum is a sum of at most k weights bounded by B, so it takes at most 2Bk+1 values; the top accumulator takes at most 2Vm+1 values. Correctness: induction over the processed variables; the state holds exactly what is needed to decide each closed gate and the final top sum. Cited premise (from memory, SOURCE-CHECK before any review): Kneis, Molle, Richter, Rossmanith (SIAM J. Discrete Math. 2009) give pw(G) <= e/5.769 + O(log n) for a graph with e edges. With e <= n this gives time 2^((log2(2Bk+1)/5.769 + o(1)) n) * poly; for B = 1, k = 2 the exponent is about 0.403 n.
structure.proved_step: LEMMA-R2K: exact #SAT for read-2, fan-in-k, weight-B THR o THR by the open-gate DP in time poly * (2Bk+1)^(pw+1) * (2Vm+1); with the cited pathwidth bound, 2^(0.41 n) for B=1, k=2. Proof in lemma field.

structure.proved_step: Windowed cut DP (refinement of S0100, does NOT close G0001/G0002). Let C = (W,t,v,T) be a THR o THR circuit on n variables with bottom gates g_j(x) = [W_j.x >= t_j], |W_ji| <= B, integer top weights v_j. For a cut i and gate j with first nonzero index < i, let s_j = sum_{l<i} W_jl x_l, and let rmin_j(i), rmax_j(i) be the sums of min(0,W_jl) and max(0,W_jl) over l >= i. Gate j is DECIDED at cut i if s_j + rmin_j(i) >= t_j (always 1) or s_j + rmax_j(i) < t_j (always 0); otherwise it is UNDECIDED. Let U = max over cuts i of the number of undecided started gates. Then #{x : C(x)=1} is computed exactly by the DP whose state is (s restricted to undecided gates, tau), where tau = sum of v_j over decided-satisfied gates, in O(n m (2Bn+1)^U (sum_j |v_j| + 1)) arithmetic operations. PROOF: (i) Invariant: after x_0..x_{i-1} are fixed, a decided gate has the same outcome for every completion, so folding its v_j into tau at the moment it is decided preserves the count of completions. (ii) An undecided gate's outcome is a function of s_j and the completion, and s_j updates additively, so the transition from cut i to i+1 is exact. (iii) Each s_j lies in [-Bn, Bn], giving at most (2Bn+1)^U x (sum|v|+1) states per cut. (iv) At i = n every gate is decided (rmin = rmax = 0), so the final answer is the sum of counts with tau >= T. Since U <= K (the cut-crossing number), this refines S0100.

Scope check: the atom count gives a 2^{(1-delta)n} time bound only when r log2(e m/r) <= (1-delta) n. For m = n^alpha (alpha > 1) and r = Theta(n) this fails, since r log2(e m/r) = Theta(n log n). structure.lemma: REPAIR (rank-r atom count, corrected scope). For m >= r >= 1 the number of sign atoms A(m, r) <= sum_{i<=r} C(m, i) <= (e m / r)^r (Buck 1943 / Cover 1965). Hence if r <= (1 - delta) n / log2(e m), then A(m, r) <= 2^{(1-delta) n}. Proof: (e m / r)^r = 2^{r log2(e m / r)}; since r >= 1, log2(e m / r) <= log2(e m); so r log2(e m / r) <= r log2(e m) <= (1 - delta) n. For m = n^alpha this is r <= (1 - delta) n / (log2 e + alpha log2 n), i.e. r = O(n / log n). SCOPE: rank r = O(n / log n), any alpha, any B. This is a counting bound only; it asserts nothing about running time.

structure.proved_step: BANDWIDTH DP for the subclass B_k of THR o THR circuits. Circuit C(x) = [sum_j v_j g_j(x) >= T], g_j(x) = [W_j . x >= t_j], with V = sum_j |v_j|. Hypothesis: there is a variable order 1..n such that every bottom support S_j = {a : W_j[a] != 0} lies in an interval of length <= k. Claim: #SAT(C) = #{x in {0,1}^n : C(x) = 1} is computed exactly in O(2^k (n + mk)(2V+1)) arithmetic operations. Proof. For 0 <= i <= n let F_i = {u <= i : u and some b > i lie in a common support}. Window lemma: if u in F_i is in a support with b > i, then since the support is an interval of length k, b - u <= k-1, so u >= b-k+1 >= i-k+2. Hence F_i is contained in [i-k+2, i] and |F_i| <= k-1. Gates with max S_j = i are evaluated right after x_i is fixed; every a in S_j with a < i lies in F_{i-1}, because a shares a support with i > i-1. A gate with empty support is constant and is added to the initial partial sum. Define the state after i steps as (y, s), where y = x restricted to F_i and s = sum of v_j g_j over gates with max S_j <= i. Any gate with max S_j > i reads only variables of F_i together with variables > i, so the future contribution depends on the past only through (y, s). Hence N_i(y, s) = #{x_1..x_i : x|F_i = y, partial sum = s} obeys a recursion from N_{i-1}, with one extension per value of x_i. The number of states is at most 2^(k-1)(2V+1). Each step extends each state twice and evaluates the gates with max = i in O(k) each, giving total O(2^k (n + mk)(2V+1)). The final count is the sum of N_n(., s) over s with s >= T. Induction on i gives correctness. Consequence: for k <= (1-delta) n and V <= poly(n), #SAT runs in 2^((1-delta) n) poly(n), a saving of 2^(delta n) over brute force. Scope: the subclass is only bandwidth-bounded; general supports (G0001) are not covered. Measurements (exploratory only): cm-2f30c476ea3447f9 (400 random instances, 0 wrong, window bound holds); cm-aede213e9c0a4c5e (thr2_evaluate, 27 tests correct, but 0.006-0.009x brute-force speed at n <= 14).

structure.lemma: Clipped-prefix split counting: for THR o THR f(x)=[sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T] with |W_ji| <= n^b and m <= n/(4(b+1)log2 n), #f is computed exactly in time poly(n,m)*2^(3n/4+1); correctness holds for all integer weights.
structure.proved_step: THEOREM (subclass SPLIT(b)). Let n >= 8, b >= 0 fixed, W integer m x n, t, v in Z^m, T in Z, with |W_ji| <= n^b and m <= n/(4(b+1) log2 n). Then #{x in {0,1}^n : f(x)=1} is computed exactly in time poly(n,m) * 2^(3n/4+1). PROOF. Let k = floor(n/2), s = n-k, x = (p,q) with p in {0,1}^k, q in {0,1}^s, and split W_j = (A_j, B_j). Let lo_j = sum_i min(0,B_ji) and hi_j = sum_i max(0,B_ji), so B_j.q lies in the integer interval [lo_j, hi_j] for every q. Let tau_j(p) = t_j - A_j.p and clip_j(tau) = min(max(tau, lo_j), hi_j+1). Step 1: for every integer tau and every q, [B_j.q >= tau] = [B_j.q >= clip_j(tau)]. If tau <= lo_j both sides are 1; if tau > hi_j both sides are 0; otherwise clip_j(tau) = tau. Step 2: put kappa(p) = (clip_j(tau_j(p)))_j. Then f(p,q) = F(kappa(p), q), where F(K,q) = [sum_j v_j [B_j.q >= K_j] >= T]. Step 3: with mu(K) = #{p : kappa(p) = K} and N(K) = #{q : F(K,q) = 1}, we have #f = sum over realised K of mu(K) N(K). Step 4 (algorithm): enumerate the 2^k prefixes and compute kappa(p) in O(mk) arithmetic time, tallying mu in a hash table; for each realised K enumerate the 2^s suffixes and evaluate F in O(ms) time; output the sum from Step 3. Correctness follows from Steps 1-3. Step 5 (time): the first phase costs O(2^k m k). The second phase costs |K*| * 2^s * O(ms), where K* is the set of realised kappa vectors. Each K_j lies in {lo_j, ..., hi_j+1}, a set of size hi_j - lo_j + 2 = sum_i |B_ji| + 2 <= s n^b + 2 <= n^(b+1) (using n >= 8). So |K*| <= n^((b+1)m) = 2^(m(b+1)log2 n) <= 2^(n/4) by the bound on m. Hence the total time is poly(n,m) (2^(n/2) + 2^(n/4) 2^(n/2+1)) = poly(n,m) 2^(3n/4+1). QED. SCOPE. Correctness holds for every integer input; the running-time bound uses the subclass only. The subclass has m = o(n) bottom gates, far below the n^alpha (alpha > 1) size regime of the Chen-Tal-Wang transfer, so no circuit lower bound follows from this speed-up. OBSTACLE for linear m: the bound |K*| <= n^((b+1)m) needs m log n <= n/4; for m = Theta(n) the product of window sizes exceeds 2^(n/2). NEXT ENRICHMENT (not proved, the next step to try): count the distinct residual functions F(K, .) rather than the distinct K; if that count is 2^(o(n)) for linear m, the same algorithm extends. Status: CLAIMED, not reviewed by another session. Measurement: thr2_evaluate sharp_sat with the code in the next experiment.

structure.lemma: Bounded-support reduction for THR o THR #SAT, exact for all integer weights. Let f(x) = [sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T], supp(j) = {i : W_ji != 0}, V2 = union of supp(j) over gates with |supp(j)| >= 2, V1 = (union of supp(j) over unary gates) minus V2, V0 = [n] minus (V1 union V2). Then #f = 2^{|V0|} * sum over y in {0,1}^{V2} of N(y), where N(y) = #{z in {0,1}^{V1} : sum_i a_i z_i >= T - S(y) - c}, a_i = sum over unary gates j on i of v_j (b1_j - b0_j), c = sum over unary gates of v_j b0_j, S(y) = sum over gates with supp in V2 of v_j [W_j.y >= t_j], and b0_j, b1_j are the values of the unary gate at x_i = 0, 1.
structure.proved_step: PROOF. Every gate is either supported in V2 (all gates with |supp| >= 2, and unary gates on V2) or a unary gate on a variable of V1; no unary gate sits on V0. A unary gate on i equals b0 + (b1 - b0) x_i with b1 - b0 in {-1,0,1}, so the top sum equals S(y) + c + sum_i a_i z_i, where y is the V2 part and z the V1 part of x. The indicator of f therefore depends only on (y,z), and the V0 bits are free, which gives the displayed formula. Algorithm: precompute once the sorted subset-sum lists of the two halves of V1 (2^{|V1|/2} entries each, O(2^{|V1|/2} poly) time). For each y (2^{|V2|} values), compute S(y) in poly(n,m) time and count pairs (l, r) with l + r >= theta(y) by a two-pointer pass over the sorted lists in O(2^{|V1|/2}) time. Total time poly(n,m) * 2^{|V2| + |V1|/2} = poly(n,m) * 2^{n - |V0| - |V1|/2}. Correctness holds for all integer weights because the formula is exact. Measured: thr2_evaluate cm-dfa09e24096b46f8 (70 tests, public, held-out and adversarial, wrong = []), with speedup below 1 for n <= 16.

structure.proved_step: Bandwidth DP for THR o THR #SAT. Setting: variables 1..n in a FIXED order that is part of the input. Bottom gate j has integer weights W_j with support S_j (nonempty), last(j) = max S_j, window L_j = max S_j - min S_j + 1. Top gate: integer v_j, integer T, f(x) = [sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T]. Let l = max_j L_j and V = sum_j |v_j|. Claim: #f = #{x in {0,1}^n : f(x)=1} is computed exactly in time O(n^2 m 2^(l-1) (2V+1)). Proof: process i = 1..n. Frontier F_i = {u <= i : u in S_j for some j with last(j) > i}. Claim |F_i| <= l-1. If u in F_i via gate j, then u >= min S_j = last(j) - L_j + 1 >= i+2-l, so F_i lies in [i+2-l, i], a set of size at most l-1. DP state after step i: (assignment to F_i, partial top sum P over gates with last(j) <= i), with the count of prefixes x_1..x_i producing it. Transition by choosing x_{i+1}: a gate with last(j) = i+1 reads only coordinates u in S_j with u <= i (which lie in F_i, since last(j) > i) and u = i+1, so its value is determined by the state and x_{i+1}; add its weighted value to P; keep F_{i+1}. Final answer = sum of counts over states with P >= T. Number of states at most 2^(l-1) (2V+1), since P lies in [-V, V]. Correctness follows by induction on i.

structure.lemma: LEMMA IW (windowed interval DP, exact for all integer weights). Setting: integers k>=1, D>=1, B>=0, n>=k. Bottom gates g_j(x) = [sum_{i=0}^{k-1} w_{j,i} x_{a_j+i} >= t_j] with 0 <= a_j <= n-k, |w_{j,i}| <= B, at most D gates per start a. Top f(x) = [sum_j v_j g_j(x) >= T], S = sum_j |v_j|. Then |f^{-1}(1)| is computed by a left-to-right DP over positions p = 0..n-1. State after reading x_0..x_{p-1}: key (c, (tau_j)_{j in A_p}), where c is the sum of v_j g_j over completed gates, A_p = gates with p-k+1 <= a_j <= p-1, and tau_j = clamp(t_j minus the read part of gate j, L_j, U_j+1), with [L_j,U_j] the range of the unread part of gate j's sum. Proof: (1) clamping preserves gate values; (2) the future depends only on the key, so equal keys can be merged; (3) U_j-L_j <= 2Bk, so tau_j takes <= 2Bk+2 values; c lies in an interval of S+1 integers; |A_p| <= D(k-1); so each level has <= (S+1)(2Bk+2)^{D(k-1)} keys; (4) each key has 2 transitions with O(Dk) updates, total O(n Dk^2 (S+1)(2Bk+2)^{D(k-1)}) integer operations. Scope: D = O(1) gives m = O(n) bottom gates, and k = n/log^2 n gives 2^{O(n/log n)} poly(n) time. This does NOT reach m = n^alpha (alpha>1), where D ~ n^{alpha-1} makes (2Bk+2)^{Dk} exceed 2^{o(n)}. Status: hand proof; finite check cm-d2d4173c81144d8e; independent review pending. A reviewer may judge it a standard path DP.

structure.proved_step: LEMMA-RO (random-order frontier DP, Las Vegas). Setting: fixed integers c,k >= 1; D = c(k-1); THR o THR circuit f = [sum_j v_j g_j >= T] with bottom gates g_j = [sum_{i in S_j} w_{ji} x_i >= t_j], |S_j| <= k, each variable in at most c supports S_j, |v_j|, |w_{ji}| at most V(n) polynomial, any number m of gates. Let beta_D = (D/(D+1)) (D+1)^{-1/D} < 1. Claim: for every eps > 0 there is a Las Vegas algorithm computing #f exactly with expected time poly(n,m,V) 2^{(beta_D+eps) n}. Proof: (1) Fix an ordering pi of variables, pos(i) its position. Gate j completes at ct_j = max pos over S_j. K_t = {i : pos(i) <= t and some gate containing i completes after t}. A DP over x restricted to K_t plus the partial sum (range at most 2mV+1 values) is exact, because variables outside K_t are no longer read by any unfinished gate. State count at most 2^{|K_t|}(2mV+1). (2) i is in K_t iff pos(i) <= t and some u in N(i) has pos(u) > t, where N(i) is the union of S_j minus i over gates containing i; |N(i)| <= D. With s = |N(i)|+1 <= D+1 and tau = t/n: P(i in K_t) = P(pos(i) <= t) - P(all of {i} union N(i) in the prefix) <= tau - C(t,s)/C(n,s) <= tau - tau^{D+1} + O(D^2/n). Maximising over tau gives E|K_t| <= beta_D n + O(D^2). (3) A transposition of two positions changes the membership of at most 2(D+1) variables, so |K_t| is 2(D+1)-Lipschitz for transpositions. A Maurey/McDiarmid-type bound for uniform permutations gives deviation eps n with probability 1 - exp(-Omega(eps^2 n / D^2)); a union bound over t <= n gives, for large n, max_t |K_t| <= (beta_D+eps) n + O(D^2) with probability at least 1/2. (4) Algorithm: sample pi, compute max_t |K_t| exactly (poly time), accept if below the threshold, otherwise resample. Expected at most 2 trials; then run the DP. The output is exact; only the running time is random. Consequence: for fixed c,k, the subclass admits a counting algorithm with running time 2^{(beta_D+eps) n} poly(n,m,V), which is a strict 2^{(1-delta)n} saving with delta = 1 - beta_D - eps > 0 for any number of gates m, including m = n^alpha. The non-literal part has at most cn/2 gates by LEMMA-OVL.

structure.lemma: Let W in Z^{m x n}, t in Z^m, and let G(x) = ([w_j . x >= t_j])_j for x in {0,1}^n. Then the number of distinct rows of the 2^n x m matrix G is at most min(2^m, sum_{i=0}^{n} C(m,i)). Proof: (a) 2^m is trivial. (b) Replace t_j by t_j - 1/2. Since w_j . x - t_j is an integer, [w_j . x >= t_j] = [w_j . x > t_j - 1/2], so every cube point lies strictly off each shifted hyperplane. Each row is therefore the sign vector of a region of the arrangement of m affine hyperplanes in R^n, and such an arrangement has at most sum_{i<=n} C(m,i) regions (Buck / Zaslavsky). Scope: integer data, any m, n. This is a bound on patterns only.

structure.proved_step: S0040 (CLAIMED, unreviewed). Setting: f(x) = #{x in {0,1}^n : sum_j v_j [<w_{idx(j)}, x> >= t_j] >= T} for m bottom gates whose weight vectors take at most d distinct values w^(1..d) in Z^n with |w^(k)_i| <= B; t_j, v_j, T arbitrary integers. Claim: f is computed exactly in O(n (2Bn+1)^d (m d + 1)) arithmetic operations. Proof: DP over prefixes. For level i let z_k = <w^(k)_{<=i}, x_{<=i}> for k = 1..d; the state is z in Z^d. Since |z_k| <= B i <= Bn, there are at most (2Bn+1)^d states per level. The transition from level i-1 to i adds b * w^(k)_i to each z_k for b in {0,1}, so the count table at level i is a function of the table at level i-1. Each gate value [<w_{idx(j)},x> >= t_j] is a function of the final z alone, so f = sum over final states z with sum_j v_j [z_{idx(j)} >= t_j] >= T of their counts. Correctness is by induction on i. Scope: polynomial time when d is constant and B is polynomial in n. GAP: this does not close G0001. General THR o THR needs d = Theta(m) (the measured thr2 family, cm-c77b7124cbc643ef, has about one form per gate), and the bound is exponential there. It is a standard, self-made subclass bound; it counts as progress only after review with confirms_closure, and it is not progress by itself.

structure.proved_step: statement: Let W be an integer m-by-n matrix with pairwise disjoint row supports S_j, each |S_j| <= c log_2 n for a fixed constant c. Let t_j,T be arbitrary integers and v_j integers with V=sum_j |v_j| <= n^C for a fixed constant C. The exact number of x in {0,1}^n satisfying sum_j v_j [sum_i W[j,i]x_i >= t_j] >= T is computable in deterministic polynomial time, specifically O(sum_j 2^{|S_j|} + m(V+1)) arithmetic operations. Proof: For each j enumerate the 2^{|S_j|} assignments to S_j and compute c_j, the number satisfying its threshold. Since supports are disjoint, each gate bit is realized by c_j assignments with bit 1 and 2^{|S_j|}-c_j with bit 0; the n-sum_j|S_j| variables outside all supports are free. Maintain D_j(q), the total multiplicity of gate patterns among the first j gates with score q, with D_0(0)=1. Update D_j(q)=(2^{|S_j|}-c_j)D_{j-1}(q)+c_jD_{j-1}(q-v_j). All reachable q lie in [-V,V], so each of m updates costs O(V+1) integer operations. The answer is 2^{n-sum|S_j|} times sum_{q>=T}D_m(q). Each table entry is at most 2^n and has O(n) bits; thus with V<=n^C and 2^{|S_j|}<=n^c, the algorithm has polynomial bit complexity.

label: G0001
statement: Item (iii) is OPEN. Web search (claude-websearch, 2026-11-21) found no source for the corollary 'no P-uniform poly-size symmetric majority circuits decide positive 1-in-3'. Anderson-Dawar (arXiv 1401.1125, STACS 2014) state that P-uniform symmetric majority circuits decide exactly the FPC-definable graph properties, with no 1-in-3 or CSP statement. Atserias-Bulatov-Dawar (ICALP 2007; TCS 2009) rule out definability in counting logic only for tractable CSPs whose variety admits a unary or affine type. The polymorphism clone of R={100,010,001} is projections only (S0001), so it has no Maltsev term and no nontrivial unary polynomial, and the ABD hypothesis is not met. Hence the cited route does not yield the corollary for positive 1-in-3, which is NP-complete. Repair needed: a different hypothesis or a different transfer for the claim.

structure.proved_step: LEMMA (control, all arities; repairs the singleton sub-step of S0019). For every k>=1, every k-ary Boolean polymorphism f of R={100,010,001} is a projection f(x)=x_i. Proof: let g(S)=f(1_S), F={S: g(S)=1}. (a) Coordinatewise application to k tuples e_{p_j} in R gives: for every ordered partition (B1,B2,B3) of [k] into possibly empty blocks, exactly one of g(B1),g(B2),g(B3) equals 1. (b) Partition (empty,empty,[k]) gives g([k])=1, g(empty)=0; partition (S,S^c,empty) gives g(S^c)=1-g(S). (c) F is intersecting: disjoint S,T in F would give two blocks with value 1 in (S,T,rest). (d) F contains [k]; let M be a minimal member. If |M|>=2, pick a in M and use the partition ({a}, M\{a}, M^c): {a} and M\{a} are proper subsets of M so not in F; g(M^c)=1-g(M)=0; all three values 0, contradicting (a). So M={i}. (e) Every S in F meets {i} by (c), so i in S. Conversely if i in S and g(S)=0 then g(S^c)=1, so S^c in F with i not in S^c, contradicting (e). Hence g(S)=[i in S], i.e. f=x_i. Scope: Boolean polymorphisms of R, all arities k>=1; Pol(R)=projections. Does not close G0001 (symmetric-majority corollary, item iii) or G0007 (constant-free closure); the idempotent route predicts all 256 relations constant-free, still open.

structure.proved_step: LEMMA (all arities). Let f:{0,1}^k->{0,1} be a polymorphism of R={100,010,001}: applying f coordinatewise to k tuples of R gives a tuple of R. Then f = x_j for some j. PROOF. Put g(S)=f(1_S) for S subset of [k]. For sigma:[k]->[3] the k rows R[sigma(1)],...,R[sigma(k)] have output coordinate i equal to f(1_{sigma^{-1}(i)}). Hence for every ordered partition (B1,B2,B3) of [k] into possibly empty blocks, exactly one Bi has g(Bi)=1 (*). Step 1: (empty,empty,[k]) gives g(empty)=0 and g([k])=1. Step 2: (S,S^c,empty) gives g(S)+g(S^c)=1. Step 3 (upward closed): if g(A)=1 and A subset B, then (A,B\A,B^c) gives g(B^c)=0, and (B,empty,B^c) gives g(B)=1. Step 4 (intersection): let g(A)=g(B)=1, X=A cap B, Y=A\B, Z=B\A. From (X,Y,A^c) and g(A^c)=0: g(X)+g(Y)=1. From (X,Z,B^c) and g(B^c)=0: g(X)+g(Z)=1. If g(X)=0 then g(Y)=g(Z)=1, but (Y,Z,rest) has two members with value 1, contradicting (*). So g(X)=1. Step 5: let M be the intersection of F={S: g(S)=1}; M is in F by Step 4, and M is nonempty since g(empty)=0. If |M|>=2, pick j in M. Then g(M^c)=0 (as M in F), g(M\{j})=0 (minimality of M), so (({j}), M\{j}, M^c) forces g({j})=1, hence M subset {j}, contradiction. So M={j}; Step 3 gives {S: j in S} subset F, and Step 2 gives equality. Thus g(S)=[j in S] and f(x)=x_j. Conversely each projection satisfies (*). QED. Every step is a finite partition check; no arity bound is used.

structure.lemma: BOUNDARY-RANK LEMMA. G finite graph, no isolated vertex (else PM=0, count:=0). E = A disjoint-union B. D = vertices incident to both A and B. a subset of A is A-valid iff a is a matching and every A-only vertex is covered by a; sigma(a) in {0,1}^D, sigma(a)_v = |a cap delta(v)|. B-valid b, tau(b) symmetric. Sigma = {sigma : exists A-valid a with sigma(a)=sigma and exists B-valid b with tau(b)=1-sigma}. Claim: for every field F, rank_F M = |Sigma| for M[a,b] = PM(a u b). Proof: (1) PM(a u b)=1 iff a A-valid, b B-valid, sigma(a)+tau(b)=1 on D (forward: a u b PM gives matching and A-only coverage, boundary cov_a+cov_b=1 with terms in {0,1}; backward: A-only covered by a, B-only by b, boundary by sigma+tau=1, disjointness gives counts add). (2) M = sum over sigma of 1_{R_sigma} 1_{C_{1-sigma}}^T, R_sigma={A-valid a: sigma(a)=sigma}, C_tau={B-valid b: tau(b)=tau}; R_sigma pairwise disjoint, C_tau pairwise disjoint. (3) Block diagonal after permutation: one all-ones block per sigma with R_sigma and C_{1-sigma} nonempty. (4) all-ones p x q block, p,q>=1, has rank 1 over every field, so rank_F M = #{sigma: R_sigma and C_{1-sigma} nonempty} = |Sigma|. Corollary: rank_F M <= 2^{|D|}. Edge cases: A or B empty (D empty, Sigma={empty} iff G has a PM); no PM (M=0); disconnected graphs and parallel edges need no hypothesis. Owner sketch step 'deg_A + deg_B = 1' is false with graph degrees; correct condition is cov_a(v)+cov_b(v)=1 on selected edges.

structure.proved_step: VTREE-EXISTENCE LEMMA (repair of the refuted all-vtree form). Statement: let G be a finite simple graph with a tree decomposition of width w. Then there is a vtree on E(G) such that for every vtree node with edge set A and complement B, rank_F M_{A,B} <= 2^(w+1) for every field F, where M_{A,B}[a,b] = PM(a union b). Proof: (1) Normalise the decomposition: give each edge e its own leaf bag {u,v} attached to a bag containing u and v; delete edge-free leaf bags; copy bags so every node has at most two children (edge leaves count as children). Validity and width w are preserved, since new bags are subsets of existing bags or copies of them. (2) Root the normalised tree T at r. For a node t let E_t be the set of edges whose leaf bag lies in the subtree of t. Build the vtree recursively: the vtree node for t has the vtree nodes of t's children as children, with a single child giving the same set. Every vtree node then has edge set E_t for some t. structure.lemma: EXACT RANK IDENTITY (cut form of S0001). Setup: finite simple graph G=(V,E), edge partition E=A⊔B. D=V(A)∩V(B), Ao=V(A)\V(B), Bo=V(B)\V(A). Valid row a⊆A: a matching covering all of Ao. Valid column b⊆B: matching covering all of Bo. Signature σ(a)∈{0,1}^D, σ(a)_v = number of edges of a at v. M[a,b]=1 iff a∪b is a perfect matching of G. Claim: for every field F, rank_F M = |Σ|, where Σ = {σ(a): a valid, some valid b has σ(b)=1−σ(a)}. Proof: (i) For valid a,b: a∪b is a PM iff every v∈D has σ(a)_v+σ(b)_v=1 (vertices of Ao,Bo are covered exactly once automatically, since a and b are matchings and do not share vertices outside D). So M[a,b]=[σ(b)=1−σ(a)], and zero rows/columns for invalid a/b. (ii) Hence row a equals the indicator χ_{1−σ(a)} of the column set {b valid: σ(b)=1−σ(a)}. Distinct signatures give disjoint column supports, so the distinct nonzero rows have disjoint supports and are linearly independent over any F; all other rows are zero or repeat these. So rank_F M = |Σ|. Corollary: rank_F M ≤ 2^{|D|}, and rank is field-independent. Parity: 2|a| = |Ao| + Σ_v σ(a)_v, so |Ao|+|σ| is even on valid rows.

structure.proved_step: SWITCHING LOWER BOUND (CLAIMED, session R1237). Setting: finite simple graph G=(V,E) with no isolated vertices; E = A disjoint-union B; D = V(A) cap V(B) (assumed nonempty); Ao = V(A)\V(B); Bo = V(B)\V(A). Valid row a: a matching inside A covering Ao. Valid column b: a matching inside B covering Bo. sigma(a) in {0,1}^D is the indicator of vertices of D covered by a. Sigma = {sigma(a): a valid and some valid b has sigma(b) = 1 - sigma(a)}. Claim: if G has a perfect matching M0 and r pairwise vertex-disjoint M0-alternating cycles C_1..C_r exist, each containing a vertex v_i in D whose two C_i-edges lie on different sides of the partition, then |Sigma| >= 2^r (hence rank_F M_{A,B} >= 2^r for every field F, by the rank identity S0001). PROOF. Step 1 (every PM splits): for a PM M, put a = M cap A and b = M cap B. Each v in Ao has all its G-edges in A, so a covers Ao, and b covers Bo likewise. For v in D exactly one M-edge meets v, and it lies in A or in B, so sigma(b) = 1 - sigma(a) on D. Hence sigma(M cap A) in Sigma for every PM M. Step 2 (flips): for S subset of [r], M_S = M0 symmetric-difference (union of E(C_i), i in S) is a PM: each vertex of C_i has one M0-edge and one non-M0 cycle edge, and flipping swaps them; vertices off the cycles are untouched. Step 3 (independent bits): v_i lies only on C_i, so the M_S-edge at v_i is the M0-edge e_i^0 if i not in S, and the non-M0 cycle edge e_i^1 if i in S. These two edges lie on different sides, so sigma(M_S cap A)_{v_i} = c_i XOR [i in S], where c_i = [e_i^0 in A]. Hence S -> sigma(M_S cap A) is injective (S and S' differ at v_i for any i in the symmetric difference), and by Step 1 its image lies in Sigma. So |Sigma| >= 2^r. QED. Consistency: each crossing vertex is in D, and |D| >= 2r, compatible with the parity bound |Sigma| <= 2^(|D|-1) (S0011, SURVIVED_REVIEW). Scope: uses only PERFECT MATCHINGS (a function in P), so the perfect-matching control applies and the lemma transfers to no non-P function.

structure.proved_step: Proof: let z=(x,y), z'=(x',y') be nonzero with disjoint supports. (1) A nonzero vertex block x_v has support of size >=2, since its coordinates sum to 0 over GF(3). Two nonzero blocks x_v, x'_v cannot both occur, because two disjoint subsets of a 3-set of size >=2 do not exist. So the vertex sets A={v: x_v != 0} and A'={v: x'_v != 0} are disjoint. (2) Both are nonempty, since x=0 forces y=0. Pick a in A and b in A'; then x_b=0 and x'_a=0. (3) y_{ab,c}=-x_{a,c} in z, so it is nonzero iff c in supp(x_a); y'_{ab,c}=-x'_{b,c} in z', so it is nonzero iff c in supp(x'_b). Both sets have size >=2 inside {0,1,2}, so they meet at some c, giving a shared support coordinate. Contradiction. Dimension: vertex rows are independent and each edge row has a private y variable, so dim = 3n - n = 2n.

structure.proved_step: Lemma R (range, c >= 1 fixed, beta > 0 fixed). There is n0(beta, c) such that for all n >= n0: 2^(beta n) / (c n) >= n. Proof. The inequality is equivalent to 2^(beta n) >= c n^2, i.e. beta n >= log2 c + 2 log2 n. (i) For n >= 16, log2 n <= sqrt(n): the function h(n) = sqrt(n) - log2 n has h(16) = 0 and h'(n) = 1/(2 sqrt n) - 1/(n ln 2) >= 0 for n >= 9 (since sqrt n >= 2/ln 2 there), so h >= 0 on [16, inf). (ii) Hence it suffices that beta n >= log2 c + 2 sqrt(n) for n >= 16. The left side is linear in n and the right side is o(n), so the set of failing n is finite; let n0(beta, c) be one more than its largest element (and at least 16). Then Lemma R holds for all n >= n0. QED. Scope: fixed beta > 0 and fixed c >= 1; the statement is asymptotic. It does not say the inequality holds for all n, and the failing set is non-empty (e.g. n = 15 for beta = 0.5, c = 1). Status: bookkeeping lemma for the MMW19 range reading, not progress toward P vs NP. Self-made and trivial: it does not count as progress under the owner rule.

structure.lemma: Finite-exception absorption (repair of the 'all n' range hypothesis in MMW19). Fix beta > 0, c >= 1, and let n0 = n0(beta,c) be the threshold from Lemma R, so that for all n >= n0, 2^(beta n)/(c n) >= n. Claim: if a one-pass streaming algorithm A decides Gap-MCSP[2^(beta n)/(c n), 2^(beta n)] (or its search version) for all n >= n0 using space S(N) and update time U(N), then there is a one-pass algorithm A' for all n >= 1 with space S(N) + K and update time U(N) + K, where K = K(beta,c) is a constant independent of n. Proof: for each of the finitely many lengths n < n0, the instance set is finite (truth tables of length 2^n < 2^n0). Hardcode the correct answers for those finitely many lengths into a fixed finite table, which costs a constant number of states. A' reads the input stream, identifies n from the input length, uses the table for n < n0 and runs A otherwise. Space and update time change by at most the constant K. QED. Scope: this removes the 'for all n' hypothesis of MMW19 for the Gap-MCSP bridge; it leaves the range condition s(n) >= n only for n >= n0(beta,c), which Lemma R supplies.

structure.proved_step: LEMMA R2 (range absorption, beta > 0 and c >= 1 fixed). There is n0(beta,c) such that 2^(beta n)/(c n) >= n for all n >= n0. PROOF. The inequality is equivalent to g(n) := beta n - log2 c - 2 log2 n >= 0. For real x > 0, g'(x) = beta - 2/(x ln 2), which is positive for x > x0 := 2/(beta ln 2). Since beta > 0, g(x) -> infinity as x -> infinity, so there is n0 >= x0 with g(n0) >= 0. g is increasing on [n0, infinity), hence g(n) >= g(n0) >= 0 for all n >= n0. QED. FINITE-EXCEPTION ABSORPTION: for n < n0 the instances of Gap-MCSP on 2^n bits form a finite set, and the set of all inputs of length < 2^(n0) is finite. A one-pass automaton that reads the stream, fixes n from the input length (length assumed known, as in MMW19), and hard-codes the answers for lengths below n0 needs K(beta,c) extra states, a constant. So A' has space S(N) + O(1) and update time U(N) + O(1). The exploratory run cm-dddc9be7ef094268 matches the analytic n0 on the grid (e.g. beta=1/2, c=1: last failure 15, n0 = 16; beta=1/2, c=2: n0 = 19).

structure.lemma: Lemma R' (explicit range threshold, all n). For beta > 0, c >= 1 and every n >= n0(beta,c) := max(16, 16/beta^2, 2*log2(c)/beta): 2^(beta n)/(c n) >= n. Proof: the claim is equivalent to beta*n >= log2 c + 2 log2 n. For n >= 16, log2 n <= sqrt(n) (equality at n=16; the derivative of sqrt(n) - log2 n is positive for n >= 9). So it suffices that beta*n >= log2 c + 2 sqrt(n). Split beta*n = beta*n/2 + beta*n/2: n >= 16/beta^2 gives beta*n/2 >= 2 sqrt(n); n >= 2 log2(c)/beta gives beta*n/2 >= log2 c. QED.

structure.proved_step: Lemma R' (analytic range threshold, all n; closes sub-item G0009(b) only). Let beta > 0, c >= 1 and n0(beta,c) := max(16, 16/beta^2, 2*log2(c)/beta). Then for every integer n >= n0: 2^(beta n)/(c n) >= n. PROOF. The claim is equivalent to beta*n >= log2(c) + 2*log2(n). (i) For n >= 16, log2(n) <= sqrt(n): equality at n = 16 (4 = 4), and d/dn[sqrt(n) - log2(n)] = 1/(2 sqrt n) - 1/(n ln 2) >= 0 whenever sqrt(n) >= 2/ln 2, which holds for n >= 9. Hence it suffices to show beta*n >= log2(c) + 2 sqrt(n). (ii) Write beta*n = beta*n/2 + beta*n/2. For n >= 16/beta^2 we have sqrt(n) >= 4/beta, so beta*n/2 >= 2 sqrt(n). For n >= 2 log2(c)/beta we have beta*n/2 >= log2(c). Adding gives beta*n >= log2(c) + 2 sqrt(n) >= log2(c) + 2 log2(n). QED. Scope: all real beta > 0, c >= 1, all integers n >= n0. Not optimal: for beta = 1/10, c = 1 the bound gives n0 = 1600, while the grid last failure is n = 140 (multiples of the denominator only).

structure.proved_step: Lemma R' (bookkeeping for G0009 a and b). For beta > 0, c >= 1 and n >= n0(beta,c) := max(16, 16/beta^2, 2 log2(c)/beta): 2^(beta n)/(c n) >= n. Proof: the claim is equivalent to 2^(beta n) >= c n^2, i.e. beta n >= log2 c + 2 log2 n. For n >= 16, log2 n <= sqrt(n) (equality at n = 16; the derivative of sqrt(n) - log2 n is positive for n >= 9). So it suffices that beta n >= log2 c + 2 sqrt(n). Split beta n = beta n/2 + beta n/2: n >= 16/beta^2 gives beta n/2 >= 2 sqrt(n); n >= 2 log2(c)/beta gives beta n/2 >= log2 c. QED. Independent replication cm-fdf69c0338614160 (exact integer test 2^(p n) >= (c n^2)^q, beta in {1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 3/4, 1/3}, c in {1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 16, 1024}, n <= 3000): zero violations at n >= ceil(n0); observed thresholds are at or below the bound (for beta = 1/2, c = 1 the last failure is n = 15, so the threshold is 16 <= 64). Scope: the lemma holds for all n >= n0(beta,c); the computation checks it on a finite grid only. This is bookkeeping and does not close any obligation in G0001-G0008.

structure.lemma: Lemma R' analytic part (bookkeeping for G0009, self-made, not progress). For 0 < beta <= 1, c >= 1 and n0 = ceil(max(16, 16/beta^2, 2 log2 c / beta)): 2^(beta n)/(c n) >= n for all n >= n0. Proof: the inequality is equivalent to beta n >= log2 c + 2 log2 n. For n >= 2 log2 c / beta, log2 c <= beta n / 2, so it suffices that g(n) = beta n - 4 log2 n >= 0. g is increasing for n >= 4/(beta ln 2), and 16/beta^2 >= 16 >= 4/(beta ln 2) for beta <= 1, so g is increasing on [n0, inf). At n = 16/beta^2, g = 16/beta - 16 + 8 log2 beta >= 0 since 16/beta >= 16 and log2 beta <= 0. Hence g >= 0 on [n0, inf). Scope: beta in (0,1] only; beta > 1 is not covered.

structure.lemma: Lemma FE (finite-exception transfer, per-oracle reading). Fix 0<beta<=1, c>=1, let n0 = n0(beta,c) be the threshold of Lemma R' (R1305), let s(n) = 2^(beta n)/(c n), and define s''(n) = s(n) for n >= n0 and s''(n) = n for n < n0. STATEMENT: (i) s''(n) >= n for every n >= 1; (ii) s'' = s for n >= n0; (iii) if a one-pass algorithm A (for a fixed oracle A) solves search-MCSP^A[s] on all input lengths with space S(n) and update time U(n), then there is a one-pass algorithm A'' for search-MCSP^A[s''] with space max(S(n), K) and update time max(U(n), K) for a constant K = K(beta,c,A) independent of n. PROOF: (i) for n >= n0 this is Lemma R' (2^(beta n)/(cn) >= n); for n < n0 it holds by definition. (ii) by definition. (iii) A'' runs A verbatim for n >= n0. For n < n0 the input has N = 2^n <= 2^(n0) bits, a constant. A'' stores the whole input (constant space) and outputs a fixed answer: the correct search output for threshold n (any valid output if no circuit of size n matches), which depends only on the finitely many pairs (n, truth table) with n < n0 and on the values of A on the finitely many oracle queries those circuits can make. These values are a constant-size advice string that depends on A and beta, c only. Since n0 is constant, K is constant. Hence any lower bound 'no one-pass poly(s'')-space, poly(s'')-update algorithm for search-MCSP^A[s'']' transfers to 'no such algorithm for search-MCSP^A[s]', because for n >= n0 the two thresholds coincide and the additive constant K does not change polynomial bounds. SCOPE: per-oracle reading only (each A gets its own constant advice). If the intended MMW19 statement requires ONE algorithm uniform over all oracles A, the advice step breaks and this is open (new sub-obligation G0003b). Also depends on MMW19 Thm 1.3 being applicable to threshold functions with s(n) >= n for all n (the form in the MMW19 intro), which is not verified at the source (G0001/G0002 remain open).

structure.proved_step: statement_start: For every finite simple graph G that is a disjoint union of even cycles and has n vertices, the Boolean perfect-matching function on edge variables has a deterministic decomposable NNF of size O(n). Proof: Write the components as cycles C_i of lengths 2k_i. Each C_i has exactly two perfect matchings, the two alternating edge sets A_i and B_i. For each matching M among these, form the term T_M that contains y_e for e in M and ¬y_e for every other edge of C_i. Set F_i=T_A_i∨T_B_i. Each term fixes all edge variables of C_i, so it accepts exactly one assignment; the two terms are disjoint, hence the disjunction is deterministic. Each term is a conjunction of distinct edge literals, so decomposable. A cycle has 2k_i literals per term, hence F_i has O(k_i) NNF nodes. Set F=∧_i F_i. Distinct components have disjoint edge-variable sets, so this conjunction is decomposable. An assignment satisfies F iff on each component it is one of that cycle's two alternating matchings, which is equivalent to being a perfect matching of G. Summing the O(k_i) sizes gives O(Σ_i k_i)=O(n).

structure.lemma: Lemma T (cut lemma, arbitrary gate semantics). Let C be a circuit over inputs x=(a,b), a in {0,1}^{n_A}, b in {0,1}^{n_B}, whose gates compute arbitrary Boolean functions of any fan-in. Let S be a set of gates closed under gate-predecessors (each gate input of a gate in S is in S or is an A-variable). Let kappa_E(S) be the number of wires into gates outside S that originate from an A-variable or from a gate in S. Then the number D of distinct rows of M_f[a,b]=f(a,b) satisfies log2 D <= kappa_E(S). Proof: each gate in S depends only on a, so the crossing-wire message m(a) in {0,1}^{kappa_E} is a function of a. Each gate outside S is a function of its in-neighbours (b-variables, A-variables, crossing wires, or outside gates), so by induction over outside gates f(a,b)=G(m(a),b). Row a is determined by m(a), hence D <= 2^{kappa_E}. If the output lies in S, f depends on a only and D=1.

structure.lemma: Lemma T' (repair of S0001, self-correction, not a review). C: circuit over x=(a,b), arbitrary gate functions of any fan-in; S: set of gates closed under gate-predecessors; kappa_E(S): number of wires into gates outside S that come from an A-variable or from a gate in S. Then log2 D <= kappa_E(S) + [output gate in S], where D = number of distinct rows of M_f[a,b]=f(a,b). Proof: if the output gate is outside S, the crossing-wire message m(a) determines f(a,b)=G(m(a),b), so D <= 2^{kappa_E}. If the output gate lies in S, f(a,b)=h(a) and the rows take at most the two values constant 0 and constant 1, so D <= 2 = 2^{kappa_E+1} when kappa_E=0 is possible.

statement: For every finite simple graph G=(V,E), the Boolean solutions (all variables in {0,1}) of the exact-one system (14)-(15) are in bijection with proper 3-colorings of G. Consequently the number of Boolean solutions equals the number of proper 3-colorings.
derivation: Given a Boolean solution, each vertex equation (14) has exactly one selected color c, defining a coloring. For each edge e={u,v} and color c, equation (15) forces y_{e,c}=1-x_{u,c}-x_{v,c}. This forced value is in {0,1} exactly when x_{u,c}+x_{v,c}<=1, which for one-hot vertex indicators is equivalent to u and v not both having color c. Requiring this for all c is equivalent to the endpoints having different colors, so the coloring is proper. Conversely, from any proper 3-coloring set x_{v,c}=1 exactly at its color and set y_{e,c}=1-x_{u,c}-x_{v,c}; properness ensures every y is Boolean and all equations hold. Both constructions are inverse because all x are fixed by the coloring and all y are forced by (15), proving a bijection.

structure.lemma: L-b1 (exact F_2 encoding of one THR gate). Let w in {0..W}^n, B = bitlength(W), K = sum_i popcount(w_i) <= nB, and t an integer. There is a system over F_2 in x_1..x_n plus aux variables with (i) every aux variable defined by one triangular equation of degree <= 2 with <= 4 monomials; (ii) the aux values are determined uniquely by x; (iii) the output bit equals [w.x >= t] for every x; (iv) number of adder aux variables A_add = 2(F+H) <= 2K + 2B + 2*ceil(log2 n), where F = full adders and H = half adders. Comparator aux: one per bit of the sum, L <= B + ceil(log2 n) + 1.
structure.proved_step: PROOF (CLAIMED). (i),(ii): full adder on bits a,b,c of column j gives s = a+b+c mod 2 (linear eq s+a+b+c=0) and carry cy = maj(a,b,c) (eq cy+ab+bc+ca=0); half adder gives s = a+b (linear) and cy = ab (one monomial). Equations are ordered by creation, so each new variable is a function of earlier ones. (iii): over Z, a+b+c = s + 2cy (resp. a+b = s + 2cy), so each step preserves sum_j 2^j * (bits in column j) = w.x. Columns are processed low to high until each holds <= 1 bit; the final bits then encode w.x exactly, and the comparator recurrence G_{j+1} = (s_j OR G_j) if t_j = 0, (s_j AND G_j) if t_j = 1, with G_0 = 1, computes [S >= t] by induction on bits from LSB. (iv): each full adder lowers the total bit count by 1 and the count starts at K, so F <= K. Within one column the loop ends after at most one half adder, and carries only move upward, so H <= number of columns. The sum is at most nW < 2^(B + ceil(log2 n)), so there are at most B + ceil(log2 n) columns, giving H <= B + ceil(log2 n) and A_add = 2(F+H) <= 2K + 2B + 2 ceil(log2 n). structure.proved_step:
statement: Lemma (count-preserving F_2 encoding of positive 1-in-3). Let F be a positive 1-in-3 formula on n Boolean variables with m clauses, each clause listing three distinct variables. For each clause C=(x_a,x_b,x_c), impose over F_2 the equation 1+x_a+x_b+x_c+x_ax_bx_c=0, interpreted on Boolean assignments. This gives a bijection between satisfying assignments of F and Boolean assignments satisfying all m equations. The system uses n variables and m equations, each of degree at most 3 with at most four nonzero monomials; each variable's equation-occurrence count equals its clause-occurrence count.
evidence: Proof: Fix a clause assignment and let k be the number of its three variables equal to 1. The left side evaluates in F_2 to 1+k+(1 if k=3, otherwise 0), reduced modulo 2. For k=0,1,2,3 these values are respectively 1,0,1,1. Thus the equation holds exactly when k=1, which is exactly satisfaction of the positive 1-in-3 clause. Applying this independently to each clause, a Boolean assignment satisfies every equation exactly when it satisfies every clause. The variable set and assignments are unchanged, so this is a bijection and preserves the number of solutions. Each equation has constant term, three linear terms, and one cubic term, hence degree at most 3 and at most four nonzero monomials. A variable occurs in exactly the equations for clauses in which it occurs, proving the occurrence claim. Consequently, if m<=c n and the formula has maximum variable occurrence Delta, the translated system has at most c n equations and maximum variable occurrence Delta.

structure.proved_step: LEMMA (structure of the MMW19 Lemma 3.1 gate tree, sub-part (i) of G0001). Setting: d >= 2, the construction of Lemma 3.1 with leaves D0_x (x in {0,1}^n, one per truth-table bit) and layers i = 1..log_d(2^n); gate G_ij = Circuit-Min-Merge(D_{i-1, jd}, ..., D_{i-1,(j+1)d-1}, intervals). (a) Every description D_{i-1,k} (i-1 >= 0) is an input of exactly one gate G_ij, namely j = floor(k/d): the blocks {jd..(j+1)d-1} are disjoint and cover the layer. (b) The output flag bit of G_ij (its first output bit) is read by the parent gate and, in the MCSP version, by the top AND gate: fan-out 2; in the search version the flag of the root is read by the output AND only. (c) Total gates = sum over layers of ceil(prev/d), which the lab check (own counting code) shows is <= 2^n/(d-1) with depth = ceil(log_d 2^n). Proof of (a),(b): read the construction text (block partition of each layer; the output gate is the AND of the first output bit of each G_ij) - a direct reading, not a new theorem. Consequence: the gate-level graph has NO reuse of intermediate descriptions, so the unfolding of the gate tree equals the tree itself; the abstract layered DAG model in cm-32ceef23cf324b42 (which assumed reuse) does not describe this construction.

structure.proved_step: LEMMA U (unfolding bound, conditional on depth; statement exact). Let C be a Boolean circuit over fan-in-2 gates with G gates, depth D (longest path in gates), and let its single output be unfolded into a formula by replicating every gate once per root-to-gate path. Then the formula has at most 2^(D+1) - 1 nodes. Consequence: if the replacement circuit for one Circuit-Min-Merge oracle gate has G' gates and depth D <= c log2 G', the unfolded formula for that replacement has size at most 2 G'^c, and summing over the at most G' replacement gates gives size at most 2 G'^(1+c). Proof: a tree of depth D with branching at most 2 has at most sum_{i=0}^{D} 2^i = 2^(D+1) - 1 nodes; the depth hypothesis gives 2^(D+1) <= 2 G'^c; the sum over gates is at most G' times the per-gate bound. Scope: fan-in 2, single output, leaves are inputs or oracle outputs treated as atoms. This does NOT establish G0001(ii): it reduces it to the depth hypothesis D <= c log2 G' for the Sigma3SAT^A replacements, which is open (see Q-052f6de3a7).

structure.proved_step: LEMMA (point-count bound for non-adaptive evaluation PIT). Let p be prime, 1 <= d < p, t >= 1, N = C(t+d, d), q = p^k, and S a finite subset of GF(q)^t. Call S a hitting set for degree d if every nonzero g in GF(p)[x_1..x_t] of total degree <= d has g(s) != 0 for some s in S. Then |S| >= N/k. PROOF: the map phi: g -> (g(s))_{s in S} from V = {g: deg g <= d} to GF(q)^S is GF(p)-linear. Its kernel is zero by the hitting property. V has GF(p)-dimension N (the monomials of total degree <= d form a basis). GF(q)^S has GF(p)-dimension k|S|. So N <= k|S|. QED. CONSEQUENCE (scope: a test that evaluates the whole circuit at each point of S, one full circuit run per point of cost s, correct on all degree-d circuits of size <= s, for s >= (d+2)N, which bounds the size of every g in V): time >= (N/k) s >= s t^d/(k d!) (1+o(1)). So no non-adaptive point-evaluation test achieves O(s t^{d-1-eps}) for fixed d, p, k. In particular the top-layer and ball tests are optimal up to a constant factor in point count. This does NOT close O-E: it is a limit on one procedure class. Any improvement must share work across points (symbolic treatment of variables, as in the O(s t^{d-1}) route of Theorem 2), or be adaptive.

If H_B contains G[K_2] (the lexicographic product, each vertex of G blown up to a 2-clique, adjacent blow-ups fully joined) as a MINOR, then tw(H_B) >= tw(G[K_2]) by minor-monotonicity of treewidth. structure.proved_step: LEMMA L-R (all bases, any finite graph G, isolated vertices allowed). Setting: clause-sum system over GF(3) with variables z(v,c) for v in V, c in {0,1,2}, and z(e,c) for e in E, c in {0,1,2}; kernel K = {z : sum_c z(v,c) = 0 for all v; z(u,c)+z(w,c)+z(e,c) = 0 for e=uw and all c}. Let B = (b_i) be ANY basis of K, so |iota| = 2|V|. H_B on iota: i~j iff some coordinate z has b_i(z) != 0 and b_j(z) != 0. For u in V let R_u = {i : the u-block (b_i(u,0), b_i(u,1), b_i(u,2)) is nonzero}. CLAIM: (a) the u-block matrix of B has rank 2; (b) |R_u| >= 2; (c) R_u is a clique of H_B. PROOF. (0) Let W = {y in GF(3)^3 : sum y = 0}. Map z -> (x_v)_v with x_v = (z(v,c))_c is injective on K (edge coordinates are forced: z(e,c) = -(x_u(c)+x_w(c))) and its image is exactly W^V (given x in W^V, define z(e,c) by that formula; vertex equations hold since x_v in W, edge equations hold by definition). (1) The projection p_u: K -> W, z -> x_u, is surjective by (0). Since B spans K, the vectors p_u(b_i) span W, which has dimension 2. This is (a); in particular at least two indices i have p_u(b_i) != 0, which is (b). (2) A nonzero y in W has at least two nonzero coordinates, since a single nonzero coordinate y_c would give sum y = y_c != 0. Two subsets of the 3-set {0,1,2} of size at least 2 always intersect. So for distinct i,j in R_u there is c with b_i(u,c) != 0 and b_j(u,c) != 0, hence i~j in H_B: this is (c). QED. SCOPE: every finite graph, every basis B, no assumption on B.

structure.proved_step: LEMMA (blow-up, repairs S0029 Claim 4): for every finite simple graph G with V nonempty, tw(G[K_2]) = 2 tw(G) + 1, where G[K_2] has vertices V x {0,1}, (u,c)~(v,d) iff (u=v and c!=d) or uv in E. PROOF. Upper: from a width-k decomposition (T,beta) of G take beta'(t)=beta(t) x {0,1}, width 2k+1; all edges and the pairs (u,0)(u,1) lie in common bags, subtrees are connected. Lower: let B be a bramble of G of order k+1 (Seymour-Thomas: tw(G)+1 = max order). Put B' = {X x {c} : X in B, c in {0,1}}. Each X x {c} is connected (G[X] connected, (u,c)~(v,c) for uv in E). Any two members touch: same X with c!=d via (u,0)~(u,1); X!=Y touching in G via a shared vertex (common (u,c)) or an edge uv (then (u,c)~(v,d) for all c,d). For a hitting set Z of B', let P_c = {u : (u,c) in Z}; Z meets X x {c} for every X, so P_c hits every X in B, hence |P_c| >= k+1 and |Z| >= 2k+2. So B' has order 2k+2 and tw(G[K_2]) >= 2k+1. QED. SCOPE: every finite simple graph with V nonempty.

structure.proved_step: Proof: (1) b_(v,a) lies in K (vertex sums 0; edge values -(z(u)+z(w)) hold since exactly one endpoint carries w_a) and {b_(v,a)} maps to the basis of T^V, so it is a basis. (2) Adjacency (some coordinate nonzero in both): w_0 and w_1 are both nonzero at colour 1, so (v,0)~(v,1) via vertex coordinate (v,1), and for uv in E all (u,a)~(v,c) via edge coordinate (uv,1); for u!=v with uv not in E no shared nonzero coordinate exists. So H_B = G[K_2] (vertices (v,a), adjacent iff v=u or uv in E). (3) Given a tree decomposition (T,beta) of G of width k, the bags beta(t) x {0,1} give a tree decomposition of G[K_2] of width 2(k+1)-1 = 2k+1. Hence min_B tw(H_B) <= 2k+1.
