structure.lemma: Balanced-node lemma. For every full binary vtree T with m >= 2 leaves, there is a non-root node v (a leaf or an internal node other than the root) with m/3 < leaves(v) <= 2m/3.
structure.proved_step: PROOF. Let S be the set of non-root internal nodes v with leaves(v) > 2m/3. Case 1: S is empty. The root's two children each have at most 2m/3 leaves and sum to m, so the larger child c has leaves(c) >= m/2 > m/3 and leaves(c) <= 2m/3. c is non-root, so it is the required node. Case 2: S is nonempty. Choose v in S with no descendant in S (deepest). Both children of v have at most 2m/3 leaves, and they sum to leaves(v) > 2m/3. The larger child c has leaves(c) >= leaves(v)/2 > m/3 and leaves(c) <= 2m/3. c is non-root, so it is the required node. Both cases give 3*leaves(v) in (m, 2m]. Finite check: exhaustive over all binary tree shapes for m = 2..10 (cm-f5ee9146624f4bec, 0 failures; counts 1,2,5,14,42,132,429,1430,4862). INDEPENDENCE NOTE: the check is by enumeration of the same shapes the proof covers, so it guards only against boundary/off-by-one errors. The proof itself is the argument above. Status: CLAIMED; needs independent review.

structure.lemma: Repair of S0010 (bounded-form DP). Let C be a THR o THR circuit on n Boolean inputs with m bottom gates g_j(x) = [w_j.x >= t_j], integer weights |w_{j,i}| <= B, top gate f(x) = [sum_j v_j g_j(x) >= T]. Suppose the bottom weight vectors take at most r distinct values u^(1),...,u^(r), with k(j) the index of gate j's form. Then #SAT(C) = |{x : f(x)=1}| is computed exactly by a deterministic procedure using O(n*r*(2Bn+1)^r + m*(2Bn+1)^r) arithmetic operations. Proof: (1) For a prefix i, define s(i) in Z^r by s_k(i) = sum_{l<=i} u^(k)_l x_l. Then |s_k(i)| <= B*i, so s(i) lies in [-Bi,Bi]^r and has at most (2Bi+1)^r <= (2Bn+1)^r values. (2) Process variables in order x_1,...,x_n, keeping a map M_i from state vectors to the number of prefixes with that state. M_0 = {0 -> 1}. Step i+1 sends each state s to s + bit*u_{.,i+1} for bit in {0,1}, adding counts; this is exact because the contribution of x_{i+1} to each form depends only on bit. Each step touches at most 2|M_i| entries, each of cost O(r). (3) At the end, g_j(x) is a function of s(n)_{k(j)} alone, namely [s_{k(j)} >= t_j]. Hence f(x) is a function of s(n) alone, and sum_x f(x) = sum_{s} M_n(s) * f(s). Evaluating f on each final state costs O(m). (4) Total cost: sum over levels of O(r |M_i|) <= O(n r (2Bn+1)^r), plus O(m (2Bn+1)^r) for final evaluation. Corollary: if r*log2(2Bn+1) <= (1-delta)n for a fixed delta>0, the running time is poly(n,m) * 2^{(1-delta)n}, a saving of 2^{delta n} over brute force. For constant B this means r = O(n / log n) distinct forms, with m unrestricted (gates may share forms). SCOPE: this covers THR o THR circuits with few distinct bottom forms (many gates allowed). It does NOT cover generic THR o THR with r = m = n^1.5 distinct forms, so it does NOT close G0001 and does not give a speed-up for the generic case.

structure.lemma: Low-rank bottom layer. Let g_j(x) = [w_j.x >= t_j] for j <= m, x in {0,1}^n, and let W = (w_j) have rank d over R. Then the bottom pattern P(x) = (g_1(x),...,g_m(x)) takes at most sum_{i=0}^{d} C(m,i) values on {0,1}^n. Proof: factor W = PQ with Q in R^{d x n}, so P(x) depends only on y = Qx in R^d. Y is finite, so choose eps below every positive gap |p_j.y - t_j|; then [p_j.y >= t_j] = [p_j.y > t_j - eps], which is a sign vector of m affine functions on R^d. The number of such sign vectors is at most sum_{i<=d} C(m,i) (Buck/Cover). The proof is checked by hand. It is an information bound on patterns, not a running time.

structure.proved_step: LEMMA (support-restricted bounded-weight DP; corrects the refuted S0010 by bounding weights and counting only the top support). Let C(x) = [sum_{j in J} v_j [w_j.x >= t_j] >= T] on x in {0,1}^n, where J = {j : v_j != 0}, integer weights |w_{j,i}| <= B, integer thresholds, integer T. Let r be the number of DISTINCT vectors among {w_j : j in J}. Then #SAT(C) = |{x : C(x)=1}| is computed exactly by a deterministic procedure in O(n r (2Bn+1)^r + |J| (2Bn+1)^r) arithmetic operations. PROOF: (1) Fix distinct forms F_1..F_r. For prefix length i and form k set s_k(i) = sum_{l<=i} F_{k,l} x_l. Then |s_k(i)| <= B i <= Bn, so s(i) lies in a set of size at most (2Bn+1)^r. (2) Let M_i(s) = #{prefixes x_{1..i} : s(i) = s}. M_0(0)=1. Then M_{i+1}(s) = M_i(s) + M_i(s - F_{.,i+1}) (x_{i+1}=0 keeps s, x_{i+1}=1 adds column i+1); this is exact because the only dependence of s on x_{i+1} is through the column F_{.,i+1}. Each step touches at most 2 |M_i| entries, each of cost O(r). (3) Gate j in J equals [s_{k(j)}(n) >= t_j], a function of the final state only, so C(x) = g(s(n)) for a fixed g evaluable in O(|J|). Hence #SAT = sum_s M_n(s) g(s), at cost O(|J|) per state. (4) Summing: O(n r (2Bn+1)^r) for the DP and O(|J|(2Bn+1)^r) for the final sum. COROLLARY: if r log2(2Bn+1) <= n - omega(log n), the time is 2^n / n^{omega(1)}; if r log2(2Bn+1) <= (1-delta) n, it is 2^{(1-delta)n} poly(n). For constant B and constant r it is polynomial. SCOPE AND LIMIT: the bound is driven by r over the top support. For generic instances with |J| ~ m ~ n^1.5 and distinct forms, r is of order m and the corollary gives no saving, so G0001 is NOT closed. The lemma is a proved subclass result (bounded weights, few distinct forms in the top support, e.g. bounded top fan-in combined with bounded B). It does not repair the generic gap. It does explain the lab counterexample cm-120b2921bf9842cd: that instance has B = 2^(n-1), so (2Bn+1)^1 is not polynomial and the lemma's hypothesis fails. Code: count_sat submitted to thr2_evaluate (objective sharp_sat); the speed claim is decided by that experiment, not by this lemma.

structure.proved_step: CLAIMED. Lemma A (few-top-gate DP, subclass). Let f(x) = [sum_j v_j [w_j.x >= t_j] >= T] on x in {0,1}^n, integer weights |w_ji| <= B, integers t_j, v_j, T. Let S = {j : v_j != 0}, k = |S|. Then #f = |f^{-1}(1)| is computed exactly in O(mn + n k (2Bn+1)^k) integer operations. Proof: (1) gates with v_j = 0 do not affect f. (2) Process x_1..x_n in order; keep N_i(p) = #{(x_1..x_i): partial sums p_j = sum_{l<=i} w_jl x_l equal p for j in S}. (3) N_0 = {0 -> 1}; N_{i+1}(q) = sum_{b in {0,1}} N_i(q - b w_{.,i+1}). (4) |p_j| <= B i <= Bn, so the table has at most (2Bn+1)^k entries; each step costs O(k) per entry per bit. (5) [w_j.x >= t_j] = [p_j >= t_j] at i = n, so #f = sum_p N_n(p) [sum_{j in S} v_j [p_j >= t_j] >= T]. (6) If k log2(2Bn+1) <= (1-delta) n the time is poly(n) 2^{(1-delta)n}; if k = O(log n) and B <= n^{O(1)} the time is 2^{O(log^2 n)} <= 2^n / n^{C} for every fixed C at large n. QED. Scope: bounded-weight, few-nonzero-top-weight subclass. Not a speed-up claim on generic instances (k ~ m ~ n^1.5 > n makes the bound vacuous).

structure.lemma: Bounded-support DP (repair of G0009(ii)). Let n >= 1, B >= 1 integers. Let g_j(x) = [w_j . x >= t_j] for j = 1..k, with w_j in {-B,...,B}^n, integer thresholds t_j, and nonzero integer top weights v_j. Let T be an integer and F(x) = [sum_j v_j g_j(x) >= T] for x in {0,1}^n. Then #F = #{x : F(x)=1} can be computed exactly in O(n k (2Bn+1)^k) arithmetic operations. Corollary: for the class with k <= c log2 n (c, B fixed; bottom gates with zero top weight dropped), the time is 2^{O(log^2 n)} = 2^{n - omega(1)}... more precisely the ratio to 2^n is n^{-omega(1)}.
structure.proved_step: PROOF. Process variables x_1..x_n in order. After i variables, the state is the vector p^(i) = (sum_{l<=i} w_{j,l} x_l)_{j=1..k}, which lies in {-Bi,...,Bi}^k, so at most (2Bi+1)^k <= (2Bn+1)^k distinct states occur. Maintain a dictionary from state to the number of prefixes reaching it. Step i+1: each state p with count c spawns p (x_{i+1}=0) and p + w_{.,i+1} (x_{i+1}=1), each with count c. This keeps the multiset of prefix-states exact by induction on i, because the final state depends only on the prefix sums. After n steps every state p gives g_j = [p_j >= t_j] for all j, so the top value is sum_j v_j g_j, and #F = sum over states with top value >= T of their counts. Each step does O(k) work per state, so the total is O(n k (2Bn+1)^k) and space is the same up to the number of states. CORRECTNESS: the count of prefixes per state is preserved, and the final test uses exactly the bottom gates' values since w_j . x = p_j after n steps. COROLLARY: if k <= c log2 n and B is constant, (2Bn+1)^k = 2^{c log2(n) log2(2Bn+1)} = 2^{O(log^2 n)}, so the total time is 2^{O(log^2 n)} poly(n), and the ratio to brute force 2^n is 2^{-(n - O(log^2 n))} = n^{-omega(1)}. SCOPE: class C(c,B) = THR o THR with at most c log2 n bottom gates of nonzero top weight and bottom weights in [-B,B]; no restriction on the number of bottom gates with zero top weight. NOT covered: generic m ~ n^1.5 bottom gates with all top weights nonzero (k = m), where the bound is (2Bn+1)^{n^1.5}, which exceeds 2^n. This does NOT close G0001 and does NOT close G0002, G0004 or G0006. Transfer status: the class uses bounded bottom weights, so it is not claimed to fall under the Williams or Chen-Tal-Wang transfer without a separate check.

structure.lemma: LEMMA (known bound, applied to cube patterns; not a new theorem). Let C be a THR o THR circuit on n Boolean variables with m bottom gates, integer weights W_j and integer thresholds t_j. Then the number of distinct bottom-output vectors (f_1(x), ..., f_m(x)) for x in {0,1}^n is at most sum_{i=0}^{n} binom(m,i). Proof: for integer data, W_j.x >= t_j iff W_j.x > t_j - 1/2, so each output is the strict sign of an affine function of x. The output vector at x is the sign label of the point x in the arrangement of the m affine hyperplanes W_j.x = t_j - 1/2 in R^n. Distinct labels occupy distinct cells, and an arrangement of m hyperplanes in R^n has at most sum_{i=0}^{n} binom(m,i) cells (Buck 1943; Zaslavsky). Gates with W_j = 0 are constant and add no hyperplane. Consequences: for m at most n the bound is exactly 2^m, so for m at most (1-delta) n it is at most 2^{(1-delta) n}; for m = n^alpha with alpha > 1 the bound is at least binom(m,n) > 2^n, so it gives no saving there.

structure.proved_step: Sized verifier lemma. Fix n, N=2^n, s>=1. Encode a fan-in-2 circuit C on n inputs with s gates as L = O(s log(n+s)) bits: each gate stores two operand indices in [0, n+s) plus a gate-type bit. Let V(f,y) be the circuit with inputs f in {0,1}^N and y in {0,1}^L that outputs 1 iff y is well-formed, decodes to a circuit C of size <= s on n inputs, and C(a)=f(a) for all a in {0,1}^n. Claim: V has size O(N*s*max(n,s)). Proof: (i) Well-formedness and decoding of y cost O(L log L) gates, which is negligible. (ii) For each of the N points a, evaluate C(a) with a universal evaluator. Keep a value bank of n+s wires (the n inputs, hard-wired as constants for a, plus the s gate outputs). Gate t computes its two operands by multiplexers over the n+s bank wires, costing O(n+s) gates per operand, then one gate. One point costs O(s*(n+s)) gates. (iii) Compare C(a) with f(a): O(1) per point. Total O(N*(s*(n+s)+1)) = O(N*s*max(n,s)). With n = log N and s <= (log N)^c for a fixed c >= 1, this is O(N*(log N)^{2c}) = N*(log N)^{O(1)}. Consequence: if a search circuit S of size N(log N)^k outputs encodings of size-<=s circuits, then Dec(f)=V(f,S(f)) is a decision circuit of size N(log N)^{k'} with k' = max(k,2c)+O(1). By S0002, Dec = MCSP[s] (E2 not used). Contrapositive: no size-N(log N)^{k'} circuit family for decision MCSP[(log N)^c] implies none for search-MCSP at size N(log N)^k. This is the direction the H1 transfer needs.

structure.proved_step: BASE CASE K=0 (proof, CLAIMED until reviewed). If K=0, every reachable node has fan-out <= 1, so the reachable subcircuit is a tree rooted at the output. Each gate has exactly two children, and every input is used at most once. A full binary tree with S internal nodes has S+1 leaves, so L = S+1 = (S+1)*2^0. Note that a gate g=(x,x) gives x fan-out 2, so it is excluded from K=0.

A correct induction needs a potential that charges p_u+1 against the shared nodes below u, or a proof that the sum over the H-paths with a fixed subset of visited shared nodes is at most (S+1). structure.lemma: Reformulation (hand argument, not a proof). Let U be the set of shared nodes (fan-out >= 2, reachable from the root r), and let each non-shared gate have a unique parent, so the private regions below shared nodes partition the non-shared gates. For shared u, let p_u be the number of gates in u's private region (including u). Its exit paths (ending at a shared node or an input) number exactly p_u + 1, since the region is a binary tree. Let m(u,y) be the number of exit paths from u to y. Then L(u) = sum_y m(u,y) L(y), with L(input) = 1, and sum_y m(u,y) = p_u + 1. So L(r) is a path count in a weighted DAG H on the K shared nodes plus inputs.
structure.refuted_approach: Induction on the children of the root for the global bound: fails because fan-outs of shared nodes are global, not local to each child (already recorded as S0032 gap).

structure.proved_step: CLAIMED (proof attempt, not reviewed) LEMMA S-6ce27138d2, two-sweep form. Setting: field GF(p); cores G_k[b] of size r_{k-1} x r_k (b in {0,1}), r_0 = r_n = 1, f(x) = G_1[x_1]...G_n[x_n] nonzero; M_k(f) = 2^k x 2^(n-k) cut matrix; c_k = rank M_k(f). Statement: after one L->R sweep (step k: rref U_k of the unfolding U with rows (a,b) = G_k[b][a], U_k = B_k R_k, set G_k[b] := rows of B_k, G_{k+1}[b] := R_k G_{k+1}[b]) and one R->L sweep (mirror image), the bond dims equal c_k for 1<=k<=n-1 and f is unchanged. Proof: (i) Each elimination step preserves f: new G_k[b] R_k G_{k+1} = U_b G_{k+1} = G_k[b] G_{k+1} because U = B R. (ii) Invariant after the L->R sweep: the prefix matrix P_k(x_1..x_k) = G_1[x_1]...G_k[x_k] (2^k x s_k) has full column rank s_k, by induction (the pivot columns of U_k are independent, so B_k has full column rank, and P_{k-1} full column rank is preserved under the map induced by B_k). Hence M_k(f) = P_k S_k gives rank M_k = rank S_k <= s_k. (iii) The R->L sweep at bond k is the mirror image of step (i), so it fixes the new bond dim as the rank of the current suffix matrix; this rank equals c_k because the L->R invariant (ii) makes the suffix rank equal the cut rank. (iv) Full column rank of the prefix (ii) is restored at bond k after step k+1 of the R->L sweep, since that step only multiplies core k by an r_k x s'_k matrix whose columns are independent (pivot columns), so P_k A keeps full column rank s'_k = c_k. Hence bond k dimension = c_k.

structure.proved_step: LEMMA (single gate, any field). Let f(x)=[w.x >= t] with integer weights, W = max_i |w_i|, and let [n] = S disjoint-union T with S, T nonempty. Let M be the 2^|S| x 2^|T| cut matrix M[a,b] = f(a,b). Then for every field F, rank_F(M) = number of distinct NONZERO rows of M, and this number is at most min(2^|S|, 2W|T|+2). Proof: row a is the indicator of R_a = {b : w_T.b >= t - w_S.a}; these supports are nested (threshold sets of one linear form). Order the distinct nonzero supports R_1 strictly-in R_2 ... strictly-in R_d and pick b_i in R_i minus R_{i-1} (R_0 empty). Then M[row R_j, col b_i] = [j >= i], unitriangular, so rank >= d; rank <= d is trivial. Bound: w_T.b lies in an integer set of size at most 2W|T|+1; nonempty threshold sets are determined by their least value, so d <= 2W|T|+1 <= 2W|T|+2. The earlier draft said 'rank = number of distinct rows' and omitted the nonzero restriction; that version is false when an all-zero row occurs (example w=(1), t=5, n=2, S={x1}: rank 0, one distinct row).

structure.lemma: Rank-r state DP. Let W in Z^{m x n}, |W_ji| <= B, rank_Q(W) = r, t in Q^m, v in Z^m, T in Z, f(x) = [sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T]. Then #SAT(f) and every sign-atom count N(A) = #{x : ([W_j.x >= t_j])_j = A} are computable in time poly(m, n, r, log B) * min(2^n, (2Bn+1)^r).
structure.proved_step: PROOF. (1) Pick r linearly independent rows, M in Z^{r x n}. Each row satisfies W_j = a_j M with a_j in Q^r; let D be a common denominator so that D a_j is integral. For s(x) = Mx, W_j.x = a_j.s(x). (2) Hence [W_j.x >= t_j] = [(D a_j).s >= D t_j], so every gate, f and the atom sigma(x) depend on x only through s(x). (3) DP: N_0(s) = [s = 0]; N_{i+1}(s) = N_i(s) + N_i(s - M_{.,i+1}), exact integer arithmetic, N_i(s) = #{(x_1..x_i) : sum_k M_{.,k} x_k = s}. (4) After i steps every coordinate of s lies in [-Bi, Bi], so at most (2Bi+1)^r states, and at most 2^i states are reachable; total cost poly(m,n,r) times bit cost, which is O(r log(Bn)) bits for D a_j and D t_j (Cramer bound), giving poly * min(2^n, (2Bn+1)^r). (5) #SAT = sum_s N_n(s) [F(s) = 1]; N(A) = sum_{s: sigma(s)=A} N_n(s). Both read the same table. QED. CONSEQUENCE: if r <= (1-delta) n / log2(2Bn+1), time = poly * 2^{(1-delta)n} = 2^n / n^{omega(1)}. This subsumes the r-distinct-forms subclass S0027 (rank <= r there), with the new bound never worse.

label: G0006
statement: G0005 RESOLVED by primary source (session R1674, claude-haiku-5-5; same family as claimant, so this is NOT a cross-family review). MMW19 (STOC 2019, people.csail.mit.edu/rrw/MCSP-MKTP-stoc19.pdf, web_read window at offset 1206): search-MCSP^A[s(n)] takes a truth table T of size N=2^n and must output a Boolean circuit for T of size at most s(n) with AND, OR, NOT, A-oracle gates, or report that no such circuit exists. A circuit of size above s is not a valid output, so on every no-instance the only correct output is the none report. Case B of S0006 is therefore supported by the definition: if k has no circuit of size <= s, D(q) must be none, but D(q)=C is a circuit. Case A is unchanged: D(q) must compute k != 0, but C computes 0 on input 0. Remaining open points for S0006: (i) the constant-0 table must have a circuit of size <= s(m) (true for s(m) >= a constant, state this in the lemma); (ii) the lemma covers linear input-independent updates over F_p only; (iii) cross-family review is still required before SURVIVED_REVIEW or REFUTED.

structure.proved_step: CLAIMED L-lin (R1, F_2-linear input-independent streaming with final-state decoder). Let N=2^m, D_s = indicator of circuit size <= s over the full binary basis, P_s = {k in F_2^N : D_s(x xor k)=D_s(x) for all x}. Any realization with state Mx+c (M in F_2^{S x N}) computing D_s on all N-bit inputs has S >= N - d_s, where d_s = dim P_s <= log2(m+s) + s*log2(16(m+s)^2). Proof: (1) ker M is contained in P_s, since state(x xor k)=state(x) when Mk=0 and the decoder reads only the state; (2) rank M >= N - dim ker M >= N - d_s and rank M <= S; (3) P_s is a subgroup containing 0, and D_s^{-1}(1) is a union of its cosets, so |P_s| <= |D_s^{-1}(1)| <= (m+s)(16(m+s)^2)^s by counting circuits.

structure.proved_step: statement: LEMMA (range bound for exact search decoders on a valid input subfamily). Let X be finite, U⊆X consist only of inputs with valid witnesses, and let q:X→Q be the final state map of a deterministic streaming realization with decoder D:Q→W∪{⊥}. Suppose each w∈W is a valid witness for at most one input in U. Then q restricted to U is injective, so |Q|≥|U|; if Q=F_p^S, then S≥ceil(log_p |U|). Proof: For each x∈U, correctness makes D(q(x)) a valid witness for x, so it is not ⊥. If q(x)=q(y), determinism gives the same decoded witness for both. By the uniqueness hypothesis this implies x=y. Thus q is injective on U, yielding the cardinality bounds. The lemma permits arbitrary deterministic updates and decoder computation. For exact truth-table search, the uniqueness condition holds when a witness computes the exact input truth table.

structure.lemma: Let c>=0, k>=1 (integer or real), eta real, A=1-c-eta, D=k(1+c)-1 (D>=0). Then for beta in (0,1]: (2+beta-eta)/(1+c) > 1+k*beta iff beta*D < A. The admissible set Adm = {beta in (0,1] : beta*D < A} satisfies: (i) D=0: Adm=(0,1] if A>0, empty if A<=0; (ii) D>0: Adm={beta in (0,1]: beta < A/D}, which contains (0, min(1, A/(D+1))] when A>0 and is empty when A<=0. Adm is nonempty iff c+eta<1, and the disjunct 3-eta>(1+k)(1+c) is redundant (it implies c+eta<1).

structure.lemma: Let c, k, eta be real, A = 1-c-eta, D = k(1+c)-1. Then there is beta in (0,1] with A - beta*D > 0 iff (c+eta < 1) or (3-eta > (1+k)(1+c)). PROOF: f(beta) = A - beta*D = (1-beta)*A + beta*(A-D), a convex combination of A and A-D for beta in [0,1]. (=>) If f(beta) > 0 for some beta in (0,1], then max(A, A-D) >= f(beta) > 0, so A > 0 or A-D > 0. Now A > 0 is c+eta < 1, and A-D = 2-c-eta-k(1+c) = 3-eta-(1+k)(1+c), so A-D > 0 is 3-eta > (1+k)(1+c). (<=) If A > 0, take beta = min(1, A/(2(|D|+1))) > 0; then f(beta) >= A - beta|D| >= A - A/2 > 0. If A-D > 0, take beta = 1. No case split on D is needed, and the literal D=0 clause of S0005 is not used. The proof is by linearity of beta -> f(beta).

The total is 2(m-1)+1=2m-1. Since 2m-1<=m^2<=m^c for m>=2 and c>=2, the membership follows. statement: Circuit-description counting lemma. Fix m,s>=1 and the fan-in-2 Boolean circuit model with m input wires, gates of types AND, OR, NOT, constants available, and one designated output wire. The number of circuits with at most s gates is at most (s+1)(m+s) [3(m+s)^2]^s. Indeed, encode a circuit by its gate count j<=s, then for each gate choose one of at most 3 types and at most (m+s)^2 predecessor choices (this overcounts NOT and constant gates), and choose the output among at most m+s wires. Summing over j gives at most (s+1)(m+s)[3(m+s)^2]^s. Consequently the fraction of m-bit Boolean functions computable by such circuits is at most (s+1)(m+s)[3(m+s)^2]^s/2^(2^m). This bound concerns circuit density only; it supplies no local cofactor classification or gate-elimination estimate for MCSP[m^c].
proof: The encoding overcounts because it allows choices of wires that may not be valid predecessors and treats all gate types as having two inputs. Every valid circuit nevertheless has at least one encoding among these descriptions. Thus the number of circuits is bounded by the number of descriptions. There are at most s+1 choices of gate count, at most 3(m+s)^2 choices per gate, and at most m+s choices of output. Divide this bound by the 2^(2^m) Boolean functions to obtain the density bound.

structure.proved_step: statement: For every integer m>=2 and Boolean function f:{0,1}^m->{0,1} with support A of size t>=1, there is a coordinate i and bit b such that the cofactor f|_{x_i=b} has support t' satisfying ceil(t/2)<=t'<=t. Its free-negation fan-in-2 AND/OR DNF has at most t'(m-1)-1 gates. Proof: For any coordinate i, write a_i=|A intersect {x_i=1}| and z_i=|A intersect {x_i=0}|. Since a_i+z_i=t, max(a_i,z_i)>=ceil(t/2); choose b attaining the maximum. The cofactor support is t'=max(a_i,z_i), at most t. On m-1 variables, each of t' minterms needs m-2 AND gates and their OR uses t'-1 gates, totaling t'(m-1)-1. This guarantees a large cofactor for a freely chosen bit, not necessarily a zero cofactor. For a prescribed zero restriction, a separate balance condition is needed; for example, if sum_{a in A}|a|<=mt/2, then sum_i z_i=mt-sum_{a in A}|a|>=mt/2, so some zero cofactor has support at least ceil(t/2).

statement: For every integer c>=2 and m>=1+ceil((c-1)/ln 2), every nonempty A subset {0,1}^m with 1<=|A|<=m^(c-1) has a one-coordinate restriction to m-1 variables whose support A' is nonempty and satisfies |A'|<=(m-1)^(c-1). Consequently its indicator has a free-negation fan-in-two circuit of at most (m-1)^c-1 gates.
proof: Put t=|A|. If t=1, fix any coordinate to the value of the unique point, leaving support size 1<=(m-1)^(c-1). If t>=2, some coordinate is nonconstant on A; otherwise all points agree coordinatewise. Restrict that coordinate to its smaller nonempty fiber, of size t'<=floor(t/2)<=m^(c-1)/2. Let q=m-1. Since q>=(c-1)/ln 2 and ln(1+1/q)<=1/q, (c-1)ln(m/q)<=(c-1)/q<=ln 2, so m^(c-1)/2<=q^(c-1). Thus 1<=t'<=(m-1)^(c-1). For r nonempty support points on q variables, OR their r minterms: with free input negations this takes at most r(q-1)+(r-1)=rq-1 gates, which is <=q^c-1.

structure.proved_step: statement: Lemma: For every fixed constant a>=0, every acyclic fan-in-2 De Morgan circuit C with S>=1 gates and r gates of fan-out greater than one satisfying r<=a log_2 S has an equivalent De Morgan formula with O(S^(a+1) log S) leaves. Proof: Let R be the reused gates. For each assignment b in {0,1}^R, pin the outputs of R to b. Every gate outside R has fan-out at most one, so the pinned output predicate expands to a formula with O(S) leaves. For each g in R, add the consistency predicate requiring b_g to equal the operation on g's predecessor values; after pinning, each predecessor is constant or expands through gates outside R to a formula with O(S) leaves. Conjoining the output predicate and all r consistency predicates gives O((r+1)S) leaves per b. OR over all 2^r assignments b. On every input exactly one b agrees with the actual values at R, so the formula computes C. Its size is O(2^r(r+1)S). Since r<=a log_2 S, 2^r<=S^a, yielding O(S^(a+1) log S).

structure.proved_step: LEMMA (rank-r DP, subclass lane D). Let U in Z^{m x r}, A in Z^{r x n} with all |A_ik| <= a, t in Z^m, v in Z^m, T in Z, and f(x) = [sum_j v_j [U_j . (A x) >= t_j] >= T] for x in {0,1}^n. Then #{x : f(x)=1} is computed EXACTLY by the DP C_0 = {0 -> 1}, C_i(y) = C_{i-1}(y) + C_{i-1}(y - A_i) (A_i = i-th column of A), followed by the sum over y of C_n(y) [top(y) >= T], where top(y) = sum_j v_j [U_j . y >= t_j]. Correctness: f depends on x only through y = Ax, so the count equals sum_y N(y) g(y) with N(y) = #{x: Ax = y} = C_n(y) by the recurrence. Cost: each support set has entries in [-i a, i a]^r, so |supp C_i| <= (2 i a + 1)^r and the total time is O(n m r (2na+1)^r) arithmetic operations on integers of O(log(n a m)) bits. Consequence: for r <= (1-eps) n / log2(2na+1) and a <= poly(n) the time is 2^{(1-eps) n} poly(n, m), a saving of 2^{eps n} = n^{omega(1)} over brute force on the subclass of THR o THR circuits whose bottom weight matrix has rank at most r. Verified only on the tested cases (405 exact checks, n <= 12, r in {1,2,3}; cm-2cd5c456ea174b3b). Scope: this is the rank class only; it does not transfer to general THR o THR of size n^alpha, so it does not by itself meet the Chen-Tal-Wang threshold.

structure.lemma: RESIDUAL-DP PROCEDURE (lane D, THR o THR bottom-layer counting). Setting: n variables split into prefix S (|S| = s) and bottom block B (|B| = q = n - s). Bottom gates j = 1..m have integer weights W_j in [-a,a]^n, thresholds t_j, output weights v_j, target T. For a prefix x_S put r_j = t_j - W_{j,S}.x_S, lo_j = sum_{i in B} min(0, W_{ji}), hi_j = sum_{i in B} max(0, W_{ji}), c = sum of v_j over {j : r_j <= lo_j}, N = {j : lo_j < r_j <= hi_j}. Then #SAT(prefix) = #{x_B in {0,1}^q : c + sum_{j in N} v_j [W_{j,B}.x_B >= r_j] >= T}. Procedure: DP over the bottom variables with state z in Z^N, z_j = partial sum of W_{j,B}.x_B; the state box has size prod_{j in N} (hi_j - lo_j + 1) <= (2aq+1)^{|N|}. Time O(q |N| (2aq+1)^{|N|}) per prefix, times 2^s prefixes.
structure.proved_step: CLAIMED: Residual-DP procedure as in lemma. Derivation: each x_B contributes to exactly one partial-sum state; gates outside N are constant on all x_B (r_j <= lo_j gives always 1, r_j > hi_j gives always 0) and contribute only through c; each coordinate of a partial sum lies in [lo_j, hi_j], giving the box bound. Corollary: if |N(x_S)| <= kappa q / log2(2aq+1) for every prefix with kappa < 1, total time is 2^{n-(1-kappa)q} poly(n).
structure.refuted_approach: Earlier claim retracted in wording: 'sparse-survivor hypothesis refuted' overstates cm-190f31ddfdd54f48, which is a finite check at n <= 10 and does not reach the regime of the corollary.

structure.lemma: NECESSARY CONDITION FOR THE RESIDUAL-DP SAVING (lane D). Setting as in S0007: prefix S (|S| = s), bottom block B (|B| = q), gate j with W_j = (W_jS, W_jB), t_j, lo_j = sum_{i in B} min(0, W_ji), hi_j = sum_{i in B} max(0, W_ji), L_j = sum_{i in S} min(0, W_ji), U_j = sum_{i in S} max(0, W_ji). Define the always-live set C = {j : lo_j < t_j - W_jS.x_S <= hi_j for every x_S in {0,1}^s}. Then (a) j in C iff t_j - U_j > lo_j and t_j - L_j <= hi_j; (b) C is contained in N(x_S) for every prefix x_S, so |N(x_S)| >= |C|. Consequently the residual-DP corollary (|N(x_S)| <= kappa q / log2(2aq+1) for all prefixes) forces |C| <= kappa q / log2(2aq+1). PROOF: (a) W_jS.x_S ranges over [L_j, U_j] and both endpoints are attained (x_S = indicator of the negative, resp. positive, weights), so the residual t_j - W_jS.x_S ranges exactly over [t_j - U_j, t_j - L_j]; it lies in (lo_j, hi_j] for all x_S iff t_j - U_j > lo_j and t_j - L_j <= hi_j. (b) If j in C, every residual lies in (lo_j, hi_j], so gate j is not clipped for any prefix and belongs to N(x_S) by definition. The consequence is immediate from (b). So the residual-DP procedure can save only on families where almost all gates are clipped for most prefixes; a family where a constant fraction of gates is in C is outside its saving regime, whatever the prefix split.
structure.proved_step: CLAIMED: necessary-condition lemma as stated (criterion (a) exact; inclusion (b) immediate). Kind LEMMA, a limit of the residual-DP class, not a closing step.

structure.lemma: Characterisation of the always-live set (sharpens G0006). Setting: THR o THR, prefix S with |S| = s, bottom block B with |B| = q, gate j with weights W_j = (W_jS, W_jB), threshold t_j, integer weights bounded by a. Let lo_j = sum_{i in B} min(0, W_ji), hi_j = sum_{i in B} max(0, W_ji), L_j = sum_{i in S} min(0, W_ji), U_j = sum_{i in S} max(0, W_ji). Let C = {j : lo_j < t_j - W_jS.x_S <= hi_j for every x_S in {0,1}^s}. Then j in C iff (t_j - U_j > lo_j and t_j - L_j <= hi_j).
structure.proved_step: CLAIMED. Proof: the values W_jS.x_S over x_S in {0,1}^s form a subset of [L_j, U_j] whose minimum and maximum are attained (at x_S = indicator of the negative, resp. positive, weights). The condition 'for all x_S, lo_j < t_j - W_jS.x_S <= hi_j' says that the set of attained residuals lies in the interval (lo_j, hi_j]. A set lies in an interval iff its minimum and maximum lie in it. The residual minimum is t_j - U_j and its maximum is t_j - L_j, so the condition is t_j - U_j > lo_j and t_j - L_j <= hi_j. Consequence: every j in C is not clipped for any prefix, so C is contained in N(x_S) for every x_S, and |N(x_S)| >= |C|. Hence the residual-DP corollary |N(x_S)| <= kappa q / log2(2aq+1) forces |C| <= kappa q / log2(2aq+1).

label: G0010
statement: The averaging bound is no obstruction when windows sit in the tails of the prefix-sum distribution: a gate whose window lies in the tail is clipped for almost every prefix, so its mass can be exponentially small in s. Such tail placements make the bottom layer nearly constant and are the easy case. The open point (G0009 case ii, G0001 iii, G0006) is therefore whether every hard instance family must place many gates with windows covering a constant fraction of prefixes. This is a family-level claim that is not yet stated or tested. No proof progress is claimed.

structure.lemma: Bookkeeping identity for the clipping route (not progress by itself). For a THR o THR gate j with prefix S (size s) and bottom block B (size q), let N_j(x_S) be the event that the gate is unclipped, i.e. lo_j less than t_j minus W_jS.x_S at most hi_j. Then the expected number of unclipped gates over uniform x_S equals the sum over gates j of the mass of the window {v : t_j minus hi_j at most v less than t_j minus lo_j} under the distribution of W_jS.x_S. Hence E|N(x_S)| is at least the sum over gates of the minimum window mass over integer thresholds t_j.

structure.proved_step: CLAIMED: Cover-DP lemma (partial repair of G0001(i), restricted form). Let W = BC + E in Z^{m x n} with B in Z^{m x r}, C in Z^{r x n}, all entries of B, C, W bounded in absolute value by M, and E nonzero only on rows R (|R| = k) and column c0. Then #{x in {0,1}^n : sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T} is computed exactly by a DP over prefix states s_i = (C x_{<i}, (W_R x_{<i}), x_{c0}). Proof: (1) for j not in R, W_j.x = sum_q B_jq (Cx)_q + E_{j,c0} x_{c0}, so the gate value depends only on (Cx, x_{c0}); for j in R it is the coordinate of W_R x; hence the final state determines every gate value and f(x). (2) Transitions: s_{i+1} is a function of s_i and x_i, so the DP is exact (sum of counts over final states with f = 1). (3) Each coordinate of Cx and W_R x lies in [-Mn, Mn], so the number of states S satisfies S <= 2 (2Mn+1)^{r+k}. Time O(n * S * m * (r+k)). Consequence: #SAT in time 2^n / n^{omega(1)} whenever (r+k) log2(2Mn+1) <= n - omega(log n). Verification: exact agreement with brute force on 40 + 60 random instances (cm-1a3e813184fc44ea, cm-af453db203f14eb8, 0 mismatches); measured state counts stay below the bound (cm-53372d1d92c24fb8: n in {6..12}, r in {1,2}, k in {0,1}, e.g. n=12, r=1, k=1: max 240 states vs bound 18818 and 2^12 = 4096). GAP: this is a restatement of the rank-plus-cover saving (G0014) with an explicit state count. It does not handle generic full-rank W, where r+k is about n and S is at least 2^n. It does not close G0001(i) for general sparse E (only E on k rows plus one column), and it does not close G0001(iii) or G0013. NOT CLOSED: no closure claimed; the step is CLAIMED until a different session reviews it.

structure.proved_step: RANK-r DP THEOREM (ALGORITHM). Setting: W in Z^{m x n}, |W_ji| <= B, rank(W) = r; integers t_j, v_j, T; f(x) = [sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T] on {0,1}^n; #SAT = #f^{-1}(1). ALGORITHM: (1) choose r rows C_1..C_r of W forming a basis of the row space (exact Gaussian elimination over Q); choose pivot columns P with C[:,P] invertible. (2) For each j put lambda_j^T = W_j[P] (C[:,P])^{-1}; then W_j = lambda_j^T C exactly (verified). Clear denominators: A_j = D*lambda_j in Z^r, TH_j = D*t_j, D a positive integer. (3) DP: table of pairs (y, cnt), start {(0,1)}; for i = 1..n replace the table by {(y,c) and (y + C[:,i], c)} with equal y merged by summing counts. (4) Output sum of cnt over table entries y with [sum_j v_j [A_j.y >= TH_j] >= T]. CORRECTNESS: y(x) = Cx, so W_j.x = lambda_j.y(x), and A_j.y >= TH_j iff W_j.x >= t_j (D > 0). By induction the table after variables 1..l holds the fibre counts of y_l = sum_{i<=l} C[:,i] x_i, so step (4) equals sum_x f(x). COMPLEXITY: |table_l| <= min(2^l, (2Bl+1)^r) since |y_{l,k}| <= B l. Time = poly(n, m, r, log B, bitsize(t,v)) * min(2^n, (2Bn+1)^r), where the bit sizes of A_j, TH_j are poly(r, log B) by Cramer's rule. COROLLARY 1: if B <= n^{O(1)} and r <= (1-eps) n / log2(2Bn+1), the time is 2^n * 2^{-eps n} * poly(n,m) = 2^n / n^{omega(1)}. COROLLARY 2: if r = o(n / log n) and B = poly(n), the time is 2^{o(n)} poly(m). m = n^alpha is arbitrary. SCOPE: exact for every W; for full-rank W the state bound is 2^n, so there is no saving. This is a counting algorithm on a restricted class, not a circuit lower bound and not a P vs NP statement. Barrier label: no barrier is relevant to a counting algorithm on a restricted class. Literature: the low-rank DP is probably folklore and has not been source-checked; the new content is the explicit bound for G0002. NEXT (enriched version, not claimed): XOR_2 o THR o THR with bottom ranks r1, r2 has the same DP over (y1, y2) in Z^{r1+r2}, time min(2^n, (2Bn+1)^{r1+r2}).

statement: PREFIX-RANK STATE BOUND (repair of S0046). Let W be an integer m x n matrix with |W_ji| <= M, let W_k be its first k columns, r_k = rank_Q(W_k) >= 1, and S_k = {W_k a : a in {0,1}^k}. Then |S_k| <= min(2^k, (2Mk+1)^{r_k}).

structure.proved_step: LEMMA (touched-column bound). Let W, L, E be integer m x p matrices with W = L + E, max|L_ij| <= M, rank_Q(L) <= r, and E_ij = 0 outside a column set C with |C| = c. (3) Ex = E_{.,C} x_C depends only on x_C, so #{Ex} <= 2^c. (4) Wx = Lambda(Rx) + Ex is a function of the pair (Rx, x_C), so #{Wx} <= #{(Rx, x_C)} <= (2Mp+1)^r 2^c. The trivial bound 2^p is also an upper bound. QED. Consequence: the thresholded prefix states [W_j x >= t_j] are functions of Wx, so the same bound holds for state counts. Asymptotically, with r = o(p / log p), M constant and c <= (1-delta) p, the state count is at most 2^{(1-delta+o(1)) p}. structure.proved_step: LEMMA (M-free rank bound on bottom patterns). Let W in Q^{m x n} have rank r, t in Q^m, and P(W,t) = {(1[W_j.x >= t_j])_{j<=m} : x in {0,1}^n}. Then |P(W,t)| <= min(2^n, sum_{i=0}^{r} C(m,i)). PROOF. Factor W = U V with U in Q^{m x r}, V in Q^{r x n} (rank r). Put z = Vx. Then W_j.x = U_j.z, so the pattern is a function of z in the finite set Z = {Vx : x in {0,1}^n} subset of Q^r. Let D = {U_j.z - t_j : j, z in Z} and delta = min{|d| : d in D, d != 0} > 0 (finite set of rationals; if D = {0} there is no sign change to track). Choose eps in Q with 0 < eps < delta and t_j - eps not equal to U_j.z for all j and z in Z (finitely many exclusions). For z in Z: 1[U_j.z >= t_j] = 1[U_j.z > t_j - eps], because U_j.z >= t_j implies U_j.z > t_j - eps, and U_j.z < t_j implies U_j.z <= t_j - delta < t_j - eps. The hyperplanes H_j = {z : U_j.z = t_j - eps} avoid Z, so each z in Z lies in an open cell of the arrangement {H_j} in R^r, and the pattern is determined by that cell. Distinct patterns come from distinct cells. Rows U_j = 0 give constant sign and define no hyperplane; dropping them leaves m' <= m hyperplanes. A central fact (Buck 1943; Zaslavsky 1975): an arrangement of m' affine hyperplanes in R^r has at most sum_{i<=r} C(m',i) <= sum_{i<=r} C(m,i) cells. Hence |P| <= sum_{i<=r} C(m,i). Also |P| <= 2^n trivially. QED. COROLLARY: sum_{i<=r} C(m,i) <= (m+1)^r = 2^{r log2(m+1)}, so for m = n^alpha and r(alpha log2 n + 1) <= (1-eps) n the number of bottom patterns is at most 2^{(1-eps)n}, for every weight size M.

structure.proved_step: ALGORITHM (rank-one block, CLAIMED, pending review). Let W in Z^{m x n} have entries bounded by M, and let J be a set of k columns with W_ij = a_i v_j for all i and j in J (rank one on J). For x = (x_J, x_rest), every bottom gate sees x_J only through z = sum_{j in J} v_j x_j in [-kM', kM'] where M' = max|v_j|, so (Wx)_i = (W_rest x_rest)_i + a_i z. Procedure: for each x_rest in {0,1}^{n-k}, compute the thresholded vector using a DP over J that counts #{x_J : z = s} for each integer s (O(k^2 M') states, O(k) steps, m gate checks per state). Output = sum over x_rest and s of count(s) * [sum_i u_i [(W_rest x_rest)_i + a_i s >= t_i] >= T]. Correctness: the summand depends on x only through (x_rest, z). Time 2^{n-k} * poly(n, m, k, M'). This is 2^{n-k} poly, strictly better than the spec's 2^{n-k/2} meet-in-the-middle bound when the weights are polynomially bounded. structure.lemma: RANK-r BOX-BOUND DP. Let W in Z^{m x n} have rank r and all |W_ji| <= B. Choose a row index set R with |R| = r whose rows form a basis of the row space, and let A = W_R (integer, |A_ki| <= B). For each j there is C_j in Q^r with W_j = C_j^T A (exact, since W_j lies in the row space). Then for all x in {0,1}^n: W_j . x = C_j . (A x). Hence #SAT f = sum_y c(y) g(y), where y = A x, c(y) = #{x : Ax = y}, g(y) = [sum_j v_j [C_j . y >= t_j] >= T]. The DP over columns i = 1..n keeps a dictionary {y: c(y)} and adds column A_i (for x_i = 0 and 1). The number of keys after step i is at most prod_k (sum_{i' <= i} |A_{k i'}| + 1) <= prod_k (||A_k||_1 + 1) <= (nB + 1)^r, because coordinate k of every partial sum lies in the integer interval [sum_i min(0, A_ki), sum_i max(0, A_ki)] of length ||A_k||_1. Also keys <= 2^n. So the total running time is poly(n, m) * min{2^n, (nB+1)^r} with exact rational arithmetic. Consequence: for r <= (1 - delta) n / log2(nB + 1), the time is 2^{(1-delta) n} * poly(n, m), i.e. a saving of 2^{delta n} / poly over brute force. This refines the earlier (2na+1)^r bound, since ||A_k||_1 <= n a.

structure.proved_step: COLUMN-DELETION RANK LEMMA. Let W in Z^{m x n} with |W_ji| <= B. Let S subset [n], |S| = s, R = [n] minus S, and suppose rank(W_R) <= r, where W_R is W with the columns in S deleted. Let A be a set of rank(W_R) rows of W_R forming a basis of its row space. Entries of A are rows of W, so |A_ki| <= B. For each row j there is C_j in Q^r with W_jR = C_j^T A (exact, since W_jR lies in the row space). For x in {0,1}^n write x = (x_R, x_S). Then W_j . x = C_j . (A x_R) + W_jS . x_S. Let c(y) = #{x_R : A x_R = y} and g(z) = [sum_j v_j [z_j >= t_j] >= T], with z_j = C_j . y + W_jS . x_S compared exactly over Q. Then #{x : g(Wx)} = sum over x_S in {0,1}^s of sum over y of c(y) g(C y + W_S x_S). The DP over the columns of R keeps the dictionary {y: c(y)} and adds column A_i for x_i in {0,1}. Coordinate k of every partial sum lies in an integer interval of length ||A_k||_1 <= |R| B, so the number of keys is at most prod_k (||A_k||_1 + 1) <= (|R| B + 1)^r, and also at most 2^{|R|}. Hence the total time is O(2^s (|R| B + 1)^r poly(m, n)) with exact rational arithmetic. Special cases: s = 0 is the rank-r DP lemma (Q-9d5ab93ad8 lemma). If W = C A + E with E having k nonzero entries in total, then deleting the at most k columns touched by E leaves a matrix of rank <= r, so s <= k and the time is 2^k (nB+1)^r poly. This beats 2^n when k + r log2(nB+1) <= (1 - delta) n.

structure.lemma: EXCEPTIONAL-ROW DP (exact). Let W in Z^{m x n} with all |W_ji| <= B. Partition the rows into a normal set N (|N| = m-k) whose submatrix W_N has rank r with a row basis R (|R| = r, A = W_R), and k exceptional rows X with block E = W_X (arbitrary, |E_qi| <= B). For each j in N there is C_j in Q^r with W_j = C_j^T A (exact). For x in {0,1}^n let s(x) = (A x, E x) in Z^r x Z^k. Then W_j . x = C_j . (A x) for j in N, and W_X x = E x, so f(x) = [sum_{j in N} v_j [C_j.(Ax) >= t_j] + sum_q v_{X,q} [(Ex)_q >= t_{X,q}] >= T] is a function of s(x) alone. Let c(y,z) = #{x in {0,1}^n : s(x) = (y,z)}. Then #SAT f = sum_{(y,z)} c(y,z) g(y,z) with g the indicator above. The column DP that adds (A_i, E_i) for x_i in {0,1} computes c exactly (induction on the prefix length). Each coordinate of y lies in an integer interval of length ||A_k||_1 and each coordinate of z in an interval of length ||E_q||_1, so the number of keys is at most prod_k(||A_k||_1+1) prod_q(||E_q||_1+1) <= (nB+1)^{r+k}, and also <= 2^n. Hence #SAT f is computed exactly in time poly(n,m) * min{2^n, (nB+1)^{r+k}} with rational arithmetic for C_j. COROLLARY: this is the rank-rho bound with rho = r+k, applied to a basis that includes the exceptional rows; it adds no saving beyond rank(W) <= r+k.

Proof as in lemma (partial-sum induction plus interval box count). structure.proved_step: LEMMA (column-deletion rank-r reduction). For W in Z^{m x n} with |W_ji| <= B and r >= 0, define rho_r(W) = min{|S| : rank(W restricted to columns [n] minus S) <= r}. Then for any thresholds t, weights v >= 0 and T, the count #SAT = #{x in {0,1}^n : sum_j v_j [W_j . x >= t_j] >= T} equals sum over x_S in {0,1}^S of #{x' in {0,1}^{[n]\S} : sum_j v_j [W'_j . x' >= t_j - W_{j,S} . x_S] >= T}, where W' = W restricted to [n]\S. Each inner count is a count for the rank-<=r matrix W' with integer thresholds, so the rank-r box-bound DP applies to it, giving total time 2^{rho} * poly(n,m) * (nB+1)^r for a set S attaining rho. PROOF: partition x = (x_S, x'); the gate condition W_j . x >= t_j is equivalent to W'_j . x' >= t_j - W_{j,S} . x_S, and the outer sum over x_S is exhaustive. The identity holds for every S, not only the minimal one; minimality only minimises the 2^{|S|} factor. Corollary (E = W - W0 with rank(W0) <= r and at most e nonzero entries): S = columns touched by E gives rho_r(W) <= e, so the cost is 2^e * poly * (nB+1)^r, and S can be found by enumerating column sets of size <= e (n^e choices), giving a promise-free algorithm of time n^{O(e)} * 2^e * poly * (nB+1)^r. This subsumes S0002 (column-supported E) and covers entrywise-sparse E.

structure.lemma: CLIPPED EXCEPTIONAL-ROW DP. W in Z^{m x n}, |W_ji| <= B; normal rows N with rank r and row basis R, A = W_R; k exceptional rows X with block E = W_X. For a prefix length p let L+_q(p) = sum_{i>p} max(0,E_qi), L-_q(p) = sum_{i>p} min(0,E_qi), and clip z_q to c_q(z,p) = clamp(z_q, t_q - L+_q(p) - 1, t_q - L-_q(p)). Then (a) #SAT f is computed exactly by the DP over keys (y_p, c(z_p,p)), where y_p = A x_{<=p} and z_p = E x_{<=p}; (b) the number of keys at step p is at most min{ 2^p, prod_k(||A_k^{<=p}||_1+1) * prod_q(L+_q(p)-L-_q(p)+2) }. Proof of (a): for any future suffix delta in [L-,L+] the indicator [z_q+delta_q >= t_q] is unchanged by clamping z_q, so keys with equal (y, clipped z) have identical future weights; the transition commutes with clipping by the same argument at p+1. Proof of (b): y-coordinates lie in integer intervals of length ||A_k^{<=p}||_1; clipped z-coordinates lie in an integer interval of length L+-L-+1. Scope: exact for any integer W; the bound improves the constant over (nB+1)^{r+k} but gives no exponent saving for fixed k, and nothing for full-rank W (G0001(iii) stays open).
structure.proved_step: Clipped DP (a)+(b) as in lemma. Exactness of (a) by the window argument; (b) by interval counting. SETTING. W in Z^{m x n}, |W_ji| <= B. Thresholds t_j in Z. Let K be a set of k rows and N its complement, with rank_Q(W_N) = r. The DP is the clipped-state DP of the record: after reading x_1..x_p its key is (cnt, tuple of (j, clipped s_j) over undecided gates), where s_j = W_j^{<=p} . x_{<=p}, cnt = number of decided-true gates, and the clip is clamp(s_j, t_j - L+_j(p) - 1, t_j - L-_j(p)). The DP is exact (record lemma (a); its proof is that the clipping preserves the decision for every suffix in [L-, L+]; I re-checked this step by hand and it holds).

CLAIM 1 (state bound). Choose r independent rows of W_N as A in Z^{r x n}; every row of W_N is U_j A with U_j in Q^r. For every p, the number of keys at step p is at most (m+1) (2pB+1)^r prod_{q in K} ((n-p)B+3).
Proof. (i) For normal j, s_j = U_j . y with y = A x_{<=p} in Z^r and |y_i| <= pB. So the set of undecided normal gates and their clipped values are functions of y, and y has at most (2pB+1)^r values. (ii) For q in K, the key either omits q, or holds a clipped value in an integer interval of length L+_q(p) - L-_q(p) + 2 <= (n-p)B + 2, since the suffix l1 mass is at most (n-p)B. That gives at most (n-p)B+3 options. (iii) cnt takes at most m+1 values. The key is a function of (cnt, y, the k clipped values), so the bound follows.

CLAIM 2 (algorithm). Run the DP forward for p = 1..n. The answer is the total weight of keys with cnt >= T, where T = ceil(m/2) (or any fixed threshold). Each step loops over at most S_p keys, 2 choices of x_p, and m gates. By CLAIM 1, S_p <= (m+1)(2nB+1)^r (nB+3)^k <= (m+1)(2nB+3)^{r+k}. Hence #SAT(THR o THR) is computed in time O(n m^2 (2nB+3)^{r+k}) with exact integer arithmetic.

CONSEQUENCE. A running time 2^{(1-eps) n} holds whenever (r+k) log2(2nB+3) <= (1-eps) n - O(log n), e.g. r + k <= (1-eps) n / log2(2nB+3) for B constant. For constant r+k it is polynomial. Note: the bound does not use min with 2^p and needs no split, so it is strictly stronger than the earlier 2^{n/2} split route.

SCOPE. Exact: the set K of exceptional rows and the rank r are arbitrary (no sparsity assumed on K). Covered: W with all but k rows in an r-dimensional row space, r + k = o(n / log n) (B constant). NOT covered: full rank (r = n, k = m - n makes the bound exceed 2^n); the bound is also not better than 2^n when r+k >= n/log2(2nB+3). Does not close G0001(iii), G0003 or G0006, and does not answer whether hard THR o THR families have r + k = o(n / log n). Not checked against brute force by me; the validator must check CLAIM 2 by computation (exact count vs brute force on random instances with k noise rows and rank r) and CLAIM 1 by counting keys.

structure.proved_step: LEMMA-BLOCK (lane D, CLAIMED). Setup: W in Z^{m x n} with |W_{j,i}| <= B; t in Z^m; v in Z_{>=0}^m; T in Z; f(x) = [sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T]. Let R subset [n], |R| = q, S = [n] minus R, and r = rank_Q(W_R), where W_R is the m x q submatrix on columns R. Claim: #{x in {0,1}^n : f(x)=1} is computable exactly in time 2^{n-q} * (2Bq+1)^r * poly(m, n, log B) arithmetic operations (exact rationals). Proof: (1) choose rows P = {P_1..P_r} with W_{P,R} a basis of the row space of W_R; each row satisfies W_{j,R} = sum_p lambda_{jp} W_{P_p,R} with unique lambda_j in Q^r, computable by Gaussian elimination in poly time. (2) For x_R in {0,1}^q set y_p = W_{P_p,R}.x_R, an integer with |y_p| <= Bq, so y lies in a set Y of size at most (2Bq+1)^r. (3) For x = (x_R, z), z = x_S: W_j.x = c_j(z) + sum_p lambda_{jp} y_p, with c_j(z) = W_{j,S}.z. Hence f(x) depends only on (z, y). (4) N(y) = #{x_R : y(x_R) = y} is computed by a DP over the q columns of R: each column adds W_{P,c} to the current states, so the state set stays inside Y, with cost O(q (2Bq+1)^r r). (5) Count = sum over z in {0,1}^{|S|} and y in Y with N(y) > 0 of N(y) * [sum_j v_j [c_j(z) + lambda_j.y >= t_j] >= T]; each term costs O(m r). Total time 2^{n-q} * (2Bq+1)^r * poly. QED. Corollary (subclass C(delta, eps)): for R of size q = delta n and rank r <= eps n / log2(2B delta n + 1), the count takes time 2^{(1-delta+eps) n} * poly(n) for constant B or B = poly(n). The case S empty (R = [n]) recovers the rank-r DP of cm-2cd5c456ea174b3b. The new content is the split: column-branching on S combined with the rank-DP on R, so the 2^{n-q} term and the (2Bq+1)^r term are both controlled.

structure.lemma: Structured-support state lemma. Let n, m, r >= 1, B >= 0 be integers. Let A be an r x n integer matrix with entries in [-B, B], U an arbitrary m x r integer matrix, and E an m x n integer matrix whose nonzero columns all lie in a fixed set T of size s. Put W = UA + E. For a prefix length p <= n, the prefix state of x in {0,1}^p is the vector (W_{j,<=p} . x_{<=p}) over j in [m]. Claim: the number of distinct prefix states over x in {0,1}^p is at most min(2^p, (2Bp+1)^r * 2^{|T cap [p]|}). Consequently, if s + r*log2(2Bn+1) <= (1-eps) n, every prefix state count is at most 2^{(1-eps) n}.
structure.proved_step: Proof. For j in [m] and x in {0,1}^p: W_{j,<=p} . x = sum_{i<=p} (sum_k U_{jk} A_{ki}) x_i + sum_{i<=p} E_{ji} x_i = sum_k U_{jk} y_k + sum_{i in T cap [p]} E_{ji} x_i, where y = A_{<=p} x_{<=p} in Z^r. So the whole state vector is a function of the pair (y, x restricted to T cap [p]). Since |y_k| <= B p, y takes at most (2Bp+1)^r values; the restriction takes at most 2^{|T cap [p]|} values. Counting pairs gives the bound; the bound 2^p is trivial. Since p <= n, (2Bp+1)^r <= (2Bn+1)^r, and 2^s (2Bn+1)^r = 2^{s + r log2(2Bn+1)} <= 2^{(1-eps) n} under the stated condition. Sanity check: with s = 0 (pure rank r) it recovers the rank-r state bound. Scope: exact, for any m; T is one fixed set for the whole matrix, not per row. Not covered: per-row k-sparse E whose supports together cover all columns (the union support is then all n columns, so s = n).

Setting: W in Z^{m x n}, |W_ji| <= B_W; t in Z^m; T in Z; a set K of exceptional rows with |K| = k; every j outside K has W_j = U_j A with U_j in Z^r and A in Z^{r x n}, |A_ic| <= B_A (rows of A fixed, the same for all normal rows). Statement: N = #{x in {0,1}^n : sum_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T} can be computed exactly by a DP whose number of states after reading x_1..x_p is at most (k+1)(2pB_A+1)^r ((n-p)B_W+1)^k. Hence N is computed in time poly(n,m) (k+1) (2nB_A+1)^r (nB_W+1)^k. In particular N is computed in time 2^{(1-eps)n} poly(n,m) whenever r log2(2nB_A+1) + k log2(nB_W+1) + log2(k+1) <= (1-eps) n. PROOF. Key after prefix p: (cnt, y = A x_{<=p}, sorted tuple of (q, s_q) for q in K undecided at p, with exact partial sums s_q = W_{q,<=p}.x_{<=p}). cnt in {0..k} counts exceptional rows already decided TRUE. A row q is decided at p when its future range [minfut, maxfut] lets it be fixed; decided-FALSE rows contribute nothing. Transition: reading x_{p+1} adds A_{.,p+1} to y and W_{q,p+1} to each undecided s_q, then decides rows. Exactness: the future count depends only on the key, because (i) decided exceptional rows are absorbed into cnt; (ii) for an undecided q the future outcome depends only on s_q; (iii) a normal row j satisfies W_j.x = U_j.(A x), so at the end it is decided by U_j.y_n >= t_j with y_n = y_p + A x_{>p}, which depends only on the key and the future bits. Counting: y lies in [-pB_A, pB_A]^r, so (2pB_A+1)^r values; for each q in K the entry is absent or s_q lies in the integer window [t_q - maxfut_q(p), t_q - minfut_q(p) - 1] of size maxfut - minfut <= (n-p)B_W, so at most (n-p)B_W+1 options; cnt gives k+1. Multiplying gives the bound. The DP is exact by (i)-(iii). SCOPE AND LIMITS: (a) needs k log2(nB_W+1) + r log2(2nB_A+1) <= (1-eps)n, so it covers rank r on all but k = o(n/log n) rows, not full-rank W (k=0, r=n fails). structure.proved_step: PREFIX-RANK STATE LEMMA (general, no factorisation). Let W be an m x n integer matrix with all entries in [-L, L], L >= 1. For 1 <= p <= n let rho_p = rank over Q of the prefix block W[:, 1..p]. Then the number of distinct prefix states {W[:,1..p] x : x in {0,1}^p} is at most min(2^p, (2Lp+1)^{rho_p}). PROOF: choose rho_p linearly independent rows R (a rho_p x p integer matrix) of the prefix block. Every other row of the prefix block is a rational combination of R, row_j = sum_i lambda_{ji} R_i, with lambda fixed by W and independent of x. So W_j,<=p x = sum_i lambda_{ji} (R_i x), and the whole state is a function of R x in Z^{rho_p}. Each entry of R x lies in [-Lp, Lp], a set of 2Lp+1 integers, so at most (2Lp+1)^{rho_p} values. The bound 2^p is trivial. Consequence: if rho_p * log2(2Ln+1) <= (1-eps) n for every prefix that is used, the state count is at most 2^{(1-eps) n}. SCOPE: this is S0081 with the hypothesis A,U,E replaced by 'the prefix rank is small'; for W of total rank r it gives rho_p <= r. It does NOT help full-rank W (rho_p = p gives only the trivial bound), and it does not handle near-low-rank W = UA+E unless the rank of W itself is small.

structure.lemma: Linear prefix-state limit. Let A be an integer m x p matrix with entries in [-B, B], rank r over Q, and let N(A) = number of distinct vectors Ax over x in {0,1}^p. Claim (a): N(A) = 2^p iff ker_Q(A) contains no nonzero vector of {-1,0,1}^p; in particular rank p implies N(A) = 2^p. Claim (b): 2^r <= N(A) <= min(2^p, (2Bp+1)^r) for every such A.
structure.proved_step: LEMMA D1 (exact linear prefix-state limit). Claim (a): A x = A y iff A t = 0 with t = x - y in {-1,0,1}^p. Every nonzero t in {-1,0,1}^p arises as x - y with x = max(t,0) and y = max(-t,0), both in {0,1}^p, and x != y. So x -> Ax is injective on {0,1}^p iff no nonzero such t lies in ker A. If rank A = p then ker A = 0, so N(A) = 2^p. Claim (b), lower bound: pick r columns S with A_S of rank r. A_S is injective on Q^r, so the 2^r vectors A x with x in {0,1}^S (zero outside S) are distinct. Claim (b), upper bound: pick r linearly independent rows R of A. Every row of A is a rational combination of R, so A = M R with M rational, hence Ax = M(Rx). Each entry of Rx lies in [-Bp, Bp], so N(A) <= #{Rx} <= (2Bp+1)^r. The 2^p bound is trivial. Consequence: any DP whose state is the linear prefix vector Ax has at least 2^{rank A} states, and full-rank prefix blocks give exactly 2^p states. The rank DP saves only when r log2(2Bp+1) < p. This identifies the exact limit of the linear-state method and corrects the earlier open reading of G0003: for linear states the full-rank case is settled negatively, so any saving must come from non-linear state (thresholds or clipping) or from a different decomposition.

structure.proved_step: LEMMA (rank-r Cramer DP, exact, no factor hypothesis). Let n, m, r >= 1, W in Z^{m x n} with rank W = r and B = max |W_ji|, B >= 1. Let t, v in Z^m and T in Z. Then N(W,t,v,T) = #{x in {0,1}^n : sum_j v_j [W_j . x >= t_j] >= T} is computable exactly in time poly(m, n, log B) * (2an+1)^r, where a = r^{(r+1)/2} B^r. PROOF. (1) Choose rows R and columns C with Q = W[R,C] nonsingular (|R| = |C| = r; exists since rank r). Put d = det Q != 0 and N := adj(Q) W[R,:] in Z^{r x n}. (2) For every row j: W[j,C] = alpha_j^T Q for alpha_j = Q^{-T} W[j,C]^T, and W[R,:] has rank r, so W_j = W[j,C] Q^{-1} W[R,:]. Multiplying by d: d W_j = c_j N with c_j := W[j,C] in Z^{1 x r}. (3) Hence for y := N x in Z^r: W_j . x >= t_j iff c_j . y >= d t_j when d > 0 (reversed when d < 0). The right side is an integer, so this test is exact. Define g_j(y) := [sign(d)(c_j . y - d t_j) >= 0]. (4) The count equals sum over y of c_n(y) * [sum_j v_j g_j(y) >= T], where c_p(y) = #{x_{<=p} : N_{<=p} x_{<=p} = y}. Each c_p is computed by the recurrence c_{p+1}(y) = c_p(y) + c_p(y - N_{:,p+1}), with states y in Z^r. (5) Bounds: |N_ki| <= r * max|minor_{r-1}(Q)| * B <= r * (r-1)^{(r-1)/2} B^{r-1} * B <= a. Hence |y_k| <= a p at prefix p, and the number of states is at most (2ap+1)^r (and at most 2^p). Total work: O(n S r + S m r) integer operations with S = (2an+1)^r, plus polynomial Gaussian elimination over Q to find R, C, Q. Correctness is exact, since every step is an identity over Z. CONSEQUENCES: (a) for constant r and B = poly(n) the time is poly(n); (b) the time is 2^{(1-eps) n} poly whenever r * log2(2an+1) <= (1-eps) n, i.e. r (log2(2n+1) + ((r+1)/2) log2 r + r log2 B + 1) <= (1-eps) n. For B = O(1) this holds for r <= c sqrt(n / log n). The lemma replaces the hypothesis 'W = UA with small A' of the CLAIMED rank-r DP, and it does not need the factor bound to be an input.

structure.lemma: Sharpened row-product bound for linear prefix states. Let A be an integer m x p matrix with rank r >= 1, let B = max |a_ij|, and let N(A) = |{Ax : x in {0,1}^p}|. Let R be any set of r rows whose restrictions are linearly independent over Q. Then N(A) <= prod_{i in R} (1 + ||A_i||_1). Consequently N(A) <= min(2^p, (1+Bp)^r), and N(A) <= 2^{(1-eps)p} whenever r <= (1-eps) p / log2(1+Bp).
structure.proved_step: L-PROD: CLAIMED. Proof. (1) Rows of R form a Q-basis of the row space, so each row k satisfies A_k = sum_{i in R} c_{k,i} A_i with rational c_{k,i}. Hence (Ax)_k = sum_i c_{k,i} (A_R x)_i, so Ax is a function of A_R x. (2) Thus N(A) <= |{A_R x : x in {0,1}^p}|. (3) For each i in R, (A_i x) is an integer in [sum_j min(a_ij,0), sum_j max(a_ij,0)], an interval of length ||A_i||_1, so it takes at most 1 + ||A_i||_1 values. (4) The image A_R x lies in the product of these intervals, which gives the product bound. (5) ||A_i||_1 <= Bp gives (1+Bp)^r; 2^{(1-eps)p} follows from r log2(1+Bp) <= (1-eps) p. structure.proved_step: THEOREM (rank-r DP). Let W in Z^{m x n} with |W_jl| <= B, rank_Q(W) = r, and let t_j, v_j, T be rationals/integers. Then N = #{x in {0,1}^n : sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T} is computed exactly in O(n * m * r * (2Bn+1)^r) rational operations on numbers of bit-size poly(n, log B). PROOF. (1) Greedily choose row indices I = {k_1..k_r} with W_{k_1..k_r} linearly independent; they span the row space of W. (2) For each j there is a unique c_j in Q^r with W_j = sum_l c_jl W_{k_l} (existence: spanning; uniqueness: independence). (3) Put s(x) = W_I x in Z^r. Then W_j.x = c_j.s(x), so [W_j.x >= t_j] = [c_j.s(x) >= t_j] depends only on s(x). Hence N = sum_s D(s) g(s), where D(s) = #{x : W_I x = s} and g(s) = [sum_j v_j [c_j.s >= t_j] >= T]. (4) DP over columns i = 1..n: D_0 = delta_0, D_i(s) = D_{i-1}(s) + D_{i-1}(s - col_i), where col_i = (W_{k_l,i})_l. This is exact. (5) For x in {0,1}^n, |W_{k_l}.x| <= Bn, so every reachable state lies in [-Bn, Bn]^r: at most (2Bn+1)^r states at each step. (6) For r <= (1-eps) n / log2(2Bn+1), (2Bn+1)^r <= 2^{(1-eps)n}. With B = poly(n) this range is r = (1-eps) n / O(log n), for any m (m enters only polynomially). The coefficient denominators have bit-size O(r log(Bn)) = poly(n), so the arithmetic overhead is polynomial. SCOPE: exact rank r only. Full rank (G0001 iii) and near-low-rank (G0001 i) are NOT covered. The bound uses only r, not the structure of the thresholds. structure.proved_step: EXTENSION (rank-r DP with s free columns). Let W in Z^{m x n} with |W_jl| <= B. Let the first s columns be arbitrary and let the submatrix W' = W[:, s+1..n] have rank_Q r. Then N = #{x in {0,1}^n : sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T} is computed exactly with at most 2^s (2Bn+1)^r reachable states per column step, i.e. O(n m r 2^s (2Bn+1)^r) rational operations. PROOF. Enumerate the prefix xs in {0,1}^s (2^s choices). For fixed xs, the prefix contribution g_j(xs) = sum_{i<=s} W_ji xs_i is a fixed integer. Apply steps (1)-(5) of S0106 to W' (rows I of W' span its row space; W'_j = sum_l c_jl W'_{k_l}; state sv = W'_I x_suffix in Z^r with |sv_l| <= B(n-s)). Then W_j.x = c_j.sv + g_j(xs), so the indicator depends only on (xs, sv). Summing the DP counts over states with the condition gives N exactly. The state count is at most 2^s (2Bn+1)^r. SCOPE: column-support perturbation only (the non-rank part is confined to s columns); it does not give the entrywise near-low-rank form W = UA + E of G0001(i), and it does not cover full rank. Saving holds when s + r log2(2Bn+1) <= (1-eps) n, e.g. s = eps' n gives r <= (1 - eps - eps') n / log2(2Bn+1). EVIDENCE: exact correctness only, cm-aac7b94520a54ee7 (80 random instances, n in 4..8, s in 0..3, r in 1..3; 0 failures; max state ratio 0.545). Timing is not cited as support. structure.lemma: L1 (weight-free sign-pattern count, rank r). Let W in Q^{m x n} have rank r >= 1, t in Q^m, sigma(x) = (1[W_j . x >= t_j])_{j<=m}. Then |{sigma(x) : x in {0,1}^n}| <= min(2^n, sum_{i=0}^{r} C(m,i)). Proof: factor W = UA (U in Q^{m x r}, A in Q^{r x n}); Y = {Ax : x in {0,1}^n} is finite; delta = min |U_j . y - t_j| over y in Y with U_j . y != t_j (delta = 1 if none); s_j = t_j - delta/2. For y in Y, U_j . y >= t_j implies U_j . y > s_j, and U_j . y < t_j implies U_j . y <= t_j - delta < s_j, so sigma(x)_j = 1[U_j . y(x) > s_j] and no Y-point lies on any hyperplane {U_j . y = s_j}. Hence sigma(x) is the sign vector of a cell of the arrangement of m affine hyperplanes in R^r; distinct cells have distinct sign vectors; the arrangement has at most sum_{i<=r} C(m,i) cells (Buck 1943 / Zaslavsky). Zero rows U_j = 0 give constant signs and do not increase the count.

structure.proved_step: Cover-rank lemma (L2, CLAIMED by this session, unreviewed). Let W = P + E over Q, rank(P) <= r, and suppose every nonzero entry of E lies in a row indexed by R or a column indexed by C. Then rank(W) <= r + |R| + |C|. Proof: let E_R be E with the rows outside R zeroed and E_C = E - E_R. The nonzero rows of E_R lie in R, so rank(E_R) <= |R|. Each nonzero entry of E_C lies outside R-rows, hence in a C-column, so rank(E_C) <= |C|. Subadditivity of rank gives rank(W) <= rank(P) + rank(E_R) + rank(E_C) <= r + |R| + |C|. The lemma is exact and general; its proof is four lines. Exact check: cm-085a13b0ab7343eb (2000 random instances, m,n <= 7, 0 failures, 594 tight equalities).

structure.proved_step: L2 (meet-in-the-middle with partition-tree range counting, constant rank r). Let W = UA with U in Z^{m x r}, A in Z^{r x n}, t in Z^m, v in Z^m, T in Z; f(x) = [sum_j v_j [U_j.(Ax) >= t_j] >= T]. Fix r >= 1 constant. Split x = (x1, x2) with x1 in {0,1}^h, x2 in {0,1}^u, h + u = n, and let Y2 = {A_2 x2 : x2 in {0,1}^u} (a weighted point set of at most 2^u points in R^r). Then #f = sum over x1 of W(Y2 + A_1 x1), where W(z) = number of points of Y2 with [U_j.(z+y) >= t_j] pattern giving F=1. Claim: the cells of the arrangement {U_j.z = t_j - U_j.(A_1x1)} partition R^r into O(m^r) cells, each triangulated into O(m^r) simplices in total (constant r), and the weighted count of Y2 in each simplex is one simplex-range-counting query (Matousek 1992 partition tree: O(N) preprocessing, O(N^{1-1/r} polylog) per query, constant r). Hence the total time is 2^u * poly(n) (preprocessing) + 2^h * m^{O(r)} * 2^{u(1-1/r)} * poly(n, L) (queries, L = bit length, arithmetic only). Balancing u = h... exactly: the two exponents are u and n - u/r; choosing u = rn/(r+1) gives time 2^{rn/(r+1)} * poly(n, L) * m^{O(r)}. For r = 1 this is 2^{n/2} (consistent with the rank-one result, Q-9d5ab93ad8 / LIT-10). For constant r it is 2^{(1-eps) n} with eps = 1/(r+1), independent of the weight magnitudes. Corollary: for r = n^{1/3} (if the constants of the partition tree are controlled) the saving is 2^{n^{2/3}}, i.e. 2^n / n^{omega(1)}; NOT claimed here (the constants grow with r).

structure.proved_step: L3 (closed sign-pattern count, any dimension; repairs gap (f) of L2 without perturbation). Statement: for any d >= 0, m >= 0 and real affine functions f_1..f_m on R^d (f_j(x) = a_j.x - t_j, a_j = 0 allowed), the set P = { (1[f_j(x) >= 0])_{j<=m} : x in R^d } has |P| <= S(m,d) := sum_{i=0}^{d} C(m,i). PROOF by induction on m, all d at once. Base m=0: |P| = 1 = S(0,d). Base d=0: R^0 is one point, |P| <= 1 = S(m,0). Step m>=1, d>=1: let P' = patterns of f_1..f_{m-1} (the projection of P) and D = {p' in P' : both (p',0) and (p',1) lie in P}. Then |P| = |P'| + |D|. Case a_m = 0: f_m has constant sign, so D is empty and |P| = |P'| <= S(m-1,d) <= S(m,d). Case a_m != 0: H = {x : f_m(x) = 0} is an affine hyperplane isomorphic to R^{d-1}. Let p' in D be realised by x with f_m(x) >= 0 and y with f_m(y) < 0. Put z = (1-s)x + s y with s = f_m(x)/(f_m(x)-f_m(y)) in [0,1); then f_m(z) = 0, so z in H. Each f_j (j<m) is affine, so f_j(z) = (1-s) f_j(x) + s f_j(y). If p'_j = 1, both terms are >= 0, so f_j(z) >= 0; if p'_j = 0, both are < 0, so f_j(z) < 0. Hence z in H realises p' under the closed convention, so D lies in the pattern set of the m-1 restricted functions on H = R^{d-1}, and by induction |D| <= S(m-1,d-1). Therefore |P| <= S(m-1,d) + S(m-1,d-1) = S(m,d) by Pascal's rule C(m-1,i)+C(m-1,i-1) = C(m,i). QED. COROLLARY (rank r): if the bottom weights are W_j = U_j.A with U_j in Z^r and A an r x n integer matrix, then the bottom vector (1[W_j.x >= t_j])_j over x in {0,1}^n takes at most S(m,r) <= (m+1)^r values (subsets of [m] of size <= r inject into {0..m}^r by sorting and zero-padding). No general position, cell perturbation or half-open convention is needed, because the argument works with the closed sets directly. Numerical check: cm-5005f106b06d4a2d (exhaustive grid, m=2..5, coefficients and thresholds in {-1,0,1}; no violation).

structure.proved_step: ALGORITHM (rank-r residual DP for THR o THR #SAT). Setting: f(x) = [sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T] on x in {0,1}^n, W in Z^{m x n} with |W_jk| <= b, rank_Q(W) = r, integers t_j, v_j, T. PROOF. (1) Gaussian elimination picks r independent rows of W, indices basis, A = those rows (integer, |A_kl| <= b), and pivot columns P (the reduced rows restricted to P are triangular with nonzero diagonal, so M = A[:,P] is invertible). (2) Every row of W lies in the row space of A, so W_j = U_j A with U_j = W_j[P] M^{-1} in Q^r. Put den_j = lcm of denominators of U_j and c_j = den_j U_j in Z^r. With z(x) = A x in Z^r: W_j.x >= t_j iff c_j.z >= den_j t_j. So f(x) is a function of z(x) only. (3) |z_k(x)| <= n b, so z ranges over a set of size S <= (2nb+1)^r. (4) DP over i = 1..n keeps, exactly, a map from partial sums z_{<i} to the number of prefixes realising them (states at most S); the update adds A_i (column i of A). At the end, sum the multiplicities of states z with f(z) = 1. This is exact. Running time: n * S * poly(r, m) arithmetic operations on integers of bit length poly(r, log(nb)), i.e. (2nb+1)^r * poly(m, n, r, log b) bit operations. CONSEQUENCES: rank r = o(n / log n) with b = n^{O(1)} gives 2^{o(n)} poly(m) time. Rank r <= kappa n / log n with constant b gives roughly 2^{kappa(1+o(1)) n}, which is 2^{(1-delta) n} for kappa small. (Probably folklore; not novelty-checked.)

structure.proved_step: LEMMA L3 (sign-pattern bound, weight-free, rank r). Let W in Z^{m x n} have rank r over Q, t in Z^m, and for x in {0,1}^n put sigma(x)_j = [W_j . x >= t_j] in {0,1}^m. Then |{sigma(x) : x in {0,1}^n}| <= sum_{i=0}^{r} C(m,i). PROOF. Choose r linearly independent rows B of W; every row satisfies W_j = C_j B with C_j in Q^r. Put s = Bx in Z^r. Then W_j . x - t_j = C_j . s - t_j. Let D >= 1 be a common denominator of all C_j, so C_j . s - t_j lies in (1/D) Z for s in Z^r. Set tau_j = t_j - 1/(2D). Then C_j . s - tau_j lies in (1/D)Z + 1/(2D), which never equals 0, so sigma(x)_j = [C_j . s > tau_j] and no lattice point lies on any hyperplane H_j = {s : C_j . s = tau_j}. Hence sigma(x) is the sign vector of the cell of the affine arrangement {H_1..H_m} in R^r containing the point Bx. The number of cells of an arrangement of m affine hyperplanes in R^r is at most sum_{i<=r} C(m,i) (Buck 1943 / Zaslavsky 1975; induction R(m,r) <= R(m-1,r) + R(m-1,r-1), R(0,r) = R(m,0) = 1, which solves to the sum). QED. SCOPE: any integer W of rank r, any integer thresholds, any n; no weight-size assumption. The bound counts distinct SIGN PATTERNS of the full input x. It is not a bound on the number of DP states of a prefix-by-prefix dynamic program, and it does not bound the number of residual functions of a prefix.

structure.proved_step: LEMMA (lane D, variable-class count, CLAIMED by the session that stated it, not yet reviewed). Let C(x) = [sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T] on {0,1}^n, with integer weights. Suppose the variables partition into D classes C_1..C_D with sizes n_d >= 1, sum n_d = n, and every i in C_d has the same weight column c_d in Z^m (W_{j,i} = c_{d,j}). Then #SAT(C) = sum over 0<=y_d<=n_d of prod_d binom(n_d,y_d) * [sum_j v_j [sum_d y_d c_{d,j} >= t_j] >= T]. Proof: the map x -> (y_d = |x intersect C_d|) is onto, the fibre over y has prod_d binom(n_d,y_d) elements, and W_j.x = sum_d c_{d,j} y_d depends only on y. The sum has prod_d (n_d+1) terms, each costing O(mD). Bound: for x >= 1, x - log2(x+1) >= 0.415 (x-1). This holds with equality at x=2, and the derivative of the left side, 0.585, exceeds that of the right side, 1/((x+1) ln 2), for x >= 2. Multiplying over d gives prod_d (n_d+1) <= 2^{n - 0.415 (n-D)}. Therefore #SAT(C) is computable in time poly(m,D) * 2^{0.585 n + 0.415 D}, a saving of 2^{0.415 (n-D)} over brute force. The saving is superpolynomial iff n - D = omega(log n). For D = O(1) the algorithm is polynomial. Measured counts agree with the bound at all six grid points (cm-b15e97e20ccf4808, cm-7e78b5662f2d4e56).

structure.lemma: RANK-r SUBCLASS (exact, scope: m x n integer matrix W with |W_jk| <= B, rank r over Q). Choose r linearly independent rows R of W, with pivot columns P such that R[:,P] is invertible. Every row satisfies W_j = lambda_j R with lambda_j = W_j[P] (R[:,P])^{-1} in Q^r, because W_j lies in the row space of R. For x in {0,1}^n put y = Rx in Z^r; then |y_k| <= B n and W_j.x = lambda_j . y. Hence #SAT = sum over y in Z^r of N(y) * [ sum_j v_j [lambda_j . y >= t_j] >= T ], where N(y) = #{x : Rx = y}. N is computed by the 0/1 DP over the n columns of R, with states y in Z^r, at most (2Bn+1)^r states, and time O(n r (2Bn+1)^r) plus O(m r (2Bn+1)^r) exact rational evaluations. Corollary: for B = O(1) and r <= eps n / log2 n, the time is 2^{(eps+o(1)) n} poly(n,m), which is a saving of 2^{(1-eps-o(1))n} = n^{omega(1)} over brute force. Proof of the corollary: r log2(2Bn+1) = (eps n / log2 n)(log2 n + O(1)) = eps n (1+o(1)).

structure.proved_step: Occurrence-2 control lemma. Let G be a loopless cubic multigraph with vertex set V (clauses) and edge set E (variables). Let F_G be the positive CNF with one exactly-one (1-in-3) constraint per vertex on its three incident edges. Then the models of F_G are in bijection with the perfect matchings of G, via T -> T (the set of true edges). Proof: T satisfies the constraint at v iff exactly one edge of T is incident to v; this holds for all v iff T is a perfect matching. Loopless ensures no clause contains the same variable twice. Parallel edges are distinct variables and are handled by the same argument.

structure.lemma: L3 (time-invariant worklist, exact). Let C be a fan-in-2 circuit with s gates whose gate indices are topological (each gate input is an input bit or a gate with smaller index). The system has state: value bits val[g], in-degree counters ind[g] (initially the number of gate inputs of g, counted with multiplicity), and a queue Q (initially all gates with ind = 0). Each step pops one gate g from Q, computes val[g] from its two inputs (input bits or already-computed values), and for each successor k of g decrements ind[k] and pushes k when ind[k] reaches 0. The step rule is the same at every step. Claim: the run performs exactly s pops and val equals C at all gates. Proof: (i) each gate is pushed exactly once, because ind[k] reaches 0 exactly once; (ii) a gate is pushed only after all its gate inputs are popped, so its inputs are already computed when it is popped; (iii) every gate reaches ind = 0, by induction on index, because its inputs have smaller index and so are eventually popped. Hence s pops, each gate computed once from correct inputs. Cost: s gate evaluations; state O(s log s) bits; update O(1) amortised per pop. Consequence for K9-D4: the factor D overhead of L1 is removed, but only by enlarging the state beyond s value bits and by random access to the static gate description. Status: CLAIMED, needs independent review.

structure.proved_step: L4 (stream order, exact, bookkeeping). Let C be a fan-in-2 circuit with s gates, and let pi list its gates once each. Consider the one-pass rule: on arrival, compute the gate from its two inputs read from value memory, with s value bits and no other state. This rule computes C correctly in s steps if and only if pi is a topological order of the gate DAG. Proof: if pi is topological, induction on position shows every arriving gate's inputs are already stored, so each value is correct and exactly s steps are used. If pi is not topological, some gate g arrives before one of its gate inputs h; when g arrives the slot of h is still empty, so the rule reads an undefined value. structure.proved_step: L5 (arbitrary labelling, exact bookkeeping). Let C be an acyclic fan-in-2 circuit with s gates, labelled in any order. Rule: at each step, among the gates not yet computed whose gate inputs are all computed (inputs of the circuit count as computed), compute the one with the smallest label. Claim: the rule is never stuck, performs exactly s steps, and every computed value equals C at that gate. Proof: let D(g) be the longest path from an input to g, so D(g) is at least 1 for gates and every gate input of g has smaller D. Suppose some gate is uncomputed at a point where the rule is stuck, and pick an uncomputed gate g of minimum D. Its gate inputs have smaller D, so they are computed, so g is ready, a contradiction. Hence the rule runs until all s gates are computed. Each step evaluates one gate whose inputs already hold correct values, so each value is correct by induction on the step count. Status: CLAIMED, needs independent review. Bookkeeping: it closes no obligation and does not by itself settle K9-D4.

structure.refuted_approach: L4 'only if' direction (a one-pass rule with s value bits computes C correctly iff the stream order is topological) is FALSE as stated. Counterexample: one input x; gates h = AND(x,x) = x and g = OR(h,x) = x; order (g,h) is not topological; with initial slot value 0, g = 0 OR x = x (correct), then h = x, so both outputs are correct for every x. The rule has no undefined marker: an unfilled slot holds an arbitrary bit. With initial value 1, g = 1 OR x is wrong at x = 0, so the outcome depends on the initial state. Surviving statement: if the order is topological, the rule is correct in s steps (L4 'if' direction, CLAIMED, needs review). A converse must quantify over circuits, or fix the initial state and require correctness for all circuits.

structure.proved_step: LEMMA (store-then-run one-pass rule, CLAIMED). Model: a fan-in-2 circuit C with s gates is presented as a stream of s records (g, op_g, in_g1, in_g2), in an arbitrary order (a permutation of gate labels), each record read once; inputs x are available by random access. Algorithm: (1) during the single pass, write each record into a table T indexed by g; each record costs O(1) update; (2) after the pass, run the L3 worklist on T with no further reads of the stream. Claim: the run returns val[g] = C(x)_g for every gate, performs exactly s pops and s pushes, and E <= 2s decrements, where E is the number of gate-to-gate edges. Proof: after the pass T is exactly the description of C under the relabelling g, so T is a fan-in-2 DAG description of C. L3's proof (i)-(iii) uses only that every gate-input edge is counted in ind, and that C is acyclic (so (iii) induction on a topological order exists); both hold. Hence the run is correct, with s pops and s pushes by L3. Cost: state O(s log s) bits (value bits plus indices and op codes per record); update O(1) per record; post-pass O(s + E) = O(s) operations with random access into T.

structure.proved_step: For f = e_s^T M_1(x_1)...M_n(x_n) e_t over any field F, with M_i(x_i) = A_i + x_i B_i and variables read once in fixed order 1..n: the commutative image is identically zero iff the non-commutative f is zero. Proof: the non-commutative expansion is sum_S c_S w_S with w_S = prod_{i in S} x_i (increasing indices) and c_S = e_s^T Y_1...Y_n e_t, Y_i = B_i for i in S and A_i otherwise; the commutative monomials prod_{i in S} x_i are distinct for distinct S, so all c_S = 0 is equivalent to f = 0. Consequence: zero-testing a commutative fixed-order ROABP reduces to non-commutative ROABP zero-testing (Raz-Shpilka 2005, deterministic poly time).

structure.proved_step: Lemma L1 (repairs S0001). Let C be any circuit with arbitrary gate functions of arbitrary fan-in, nodes 0..N-1 = input variables and gates in topological order, output node f. Let A be a set of variables with complement B. Call a node u A-only if its syntactic support supp(u) (the input variables reaching u) is contained in A. Let W = {edges (u,v): u A-only, v not A-only} and kappa = |W|. Then rank_Q M_A(f) <= 2^kappa, so log2 rank <= kappa. Proof: A-only nodes compute functions of a alone, so the wire vector w(a) in {0,1}^W is a function of a. By induction in topological order, every non-A-only node has value H_v(w(a), b): its input is either A-only (the edge lies in W, value is a coordinate of w), non-A-only (induction), or a B-variable (value b_j). Constant nodes have empty support and are A-only. If the output is A-only, f depends on a only and rank = 1 <= 2^0. Rows with equal w(a) coincide, so M_A has at most 2^kappa distinct rows. QED. Lemma L2 (span bound). Fix a variable order pi, let m(u) be the largest pi-position of a variable in supp(u) (0 if empty), and let A_i be the first i variables, i = 1..N-1. Since supp(u) is contained in supp(v) for every edge u->v, the edge (u,v) lies in W_i iff m(u) <= i < m(v). Hence sum_i kappa_i <= (N-1)|E(C)|, and Lambda(pi) <= (N-1)|E(C)|. For B_2 circuits |E| <= 2 size, so Lambda(pi) <= 2(N-1) size. For unbounded fan-in or oracle gates |E| is not bounded by size. Consequence: s >= min_pi Lambda(pi) / (2(N-1)) for B_2. For IP_n with Lambda = Theta(n) this gives only s >= Omega(1). Dispute reading (K9-D3): L1 and L2 use no gate-type information, so the same inequality holds for D_orc; the only difference between B_2 and D_orc is that |E| is linear in size for B_2 and not for unbounded fan-in. Both positions stay open.
