structure.lemma: General fact (any 0/1 matrix M with n columns): let V = row space of M over Q, r = dim V = rank_Q M. Then the number of distinct rows of M is at most 2^r. Corollary for cut-width: W_OBDD(F) <= 2^{W_rank(F)}, where W_OBDD and W_rank are the min over variable orders of the max over cuts of distinct residual rows and of cut rank. Hence log2 W_OBDD <= W_rank <= W_OBDD.
structure.proved_step: PROOF. Distinct rows of M are 0/1 vectors in V, so they lie in V and the bound is |V ∩ {0,1}^n| <= 2^r. Let B be an r x n matrix whose rows are a basis of V. B has rank r, so it has r linearly independent columns; let S be their index set, |S| = r. For v = cB in V (c in Q^r), v_S = c B_S, and B_S is invertible, so c is determined by v_S and hence v is determined by v_S. So the restriction x -> x_S is injective on V. It maps V ∩ {0,1}^n into {0,1}^S, which has 2^r elements. Hence |V ∩ {0,1}^n| <= 2^r. For the corollary: fix an order pi that attains W_rank. Every cut k has distinct-row count <= 2^{rank_k} <= 2^{W_rank}, so the max over cuts is <= 2^{W_rank}; minimising over orders gives W_OBDD <= 2^{W_rank}. Check: F={x0+x1+x2=1} has W_rank=2, W_OBDD=3 <= 4. The lemma is elementary and is probably standard in the rank-versus-OBDD literature; it is recorded as a verified finite-scope step, not as new. structure.proved_step: SHARPNESS LEMMA (linear algebra, not a lower bound; barrier check: not applicable, no complexity claim). Let MUX_r on n=r+s variables (s=ceil(log2 r)) be f(d,sel)=d[sel mod r], and take the cut after the r data variables. Rows are indexed by d in {0,1}^r and the row is A d, where A is a 2^s x r 0/1 matrix with A[sel,i]=[sel mod r = i]. Each column i of A is nonzero (sel=i, valid since i<r<=2^s) and the columns have disjoint supports, so A has rank r over Q, hence d -> A d is injective. Therefore the cut has exactly 2^r distinct rows and Q-rank r, i.e. #distinct = 2^{rank_Q} holds with equality for every r>=1. Consequence: the per-cut bound of S0003 cannot be improved in general; any improvement of W_OBDD <= 2^{W_rank} must use the minimum over orders. structure.lemma: L1 (clipped partial-sum DP for a fixed number of bottom gates). Let f(x) = [sum_{j<=k} v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T] on x in {0,1}^n, with integer weights |W_ji| <= B, integer t_j, v_j, T, and k fixed. Then #f^{-1}(1) is computed exactly in O(k n (Bn+2)^k) arithmetic operations.
structure.proved_step: Proof. Let s_j(i) be the partial sum of gate j over the first i variables. Let P_j(i) = sum_{l>i} max(W_jl,0) and N_j(i) = sum_{l>i} min(W_jl,0), so the final sum lies in [s_j+N_j, s_j+P_j]. Define the class kappa_j(s) = 0 if s+P_j(i) < t_j; 1 if s+N_j(i) >= t_j; and the exact value s otherwise. (1) Exactness: for class 0 or 1 the bottom bit is the same for every completion of the remaining variables; for an undecided s the class is the exact value. So the bit vector of any completion depends only on the class vector. (2) Transitions are well defined: reading x_{i+1} changes P and N by subtracting max(W,0) and min(W,0) at index i+1. If class 0, then s'+P(i+1) <= s+P(i) < t, so s' stays class 0. Class 1 is symmetric. Undecided values are updated exactly. So the class vector at stage i+1 is a function of the class vector at stage i and x_{i+1}. (3) Counting: the DP c_{i+1}(kappa') = sum over (kappa, x_{i+1}) with transition kappa -> kappa' of c_i(kappa) is exact, and at i = n the classes are bits, so #f^{-1}(1) = sum of c_n over class vectors with top(bits) = 1. (4) State bound: at stage i an undecided value of gate j lies in an interval of length P_j(i) - N_j(i) = sum_{l>i}|W_jl| <= B(n-i), so there are at most B(n-i)+2 classes per gate and at most prod_j (B(n-i)+2) class vectors. Summing over i gives O(k n (Bn+2)^k) operations. Scope: fixed k, bounded integer weights; all other bottom gates are irrelevant to f and drop out. Compared with the plain partial-sum DP (state bound (2Bi+1)^k at stage i), the gain is a constant-factor change in the window, not a change of the exponent. Barrier and transfer check: this is a poly(n) algorithm for constant k and B = poly(n), so it cannot transfer to a 2^n/n^{omega(1)} lower-bound hypothesis; no LOWER_BOUND is claimed. Known-type status: counting for a constant number of halfspaces over a bounded-weight cube is standard (Dyer / Frieze-style pseudo-polynomial DP); I have not checked the literature, so novelty is unverified.

structure.proved_step: L-HWB-RANK (CLAIMED, derived in session R1498; needs review by another model family). Setup: HWB_n(x)=x_{|x|} for |x|>=1, 0 for |x|=0. Fix p in {0..n}, a=(x_1..x_p), b=(x_{p+1}..x_n), M_p[a,b]=HWB_n(a,b). Claim: rank_Q(M_p) <= (p+1)^2 <= (n+1)^2. Proof: HWB(x)=sum_{t=1}^n [|x|=t] x_t. Put s=|a|. For t<=p the term is a_t [|b|=t-s]; for t>p it is [|b|=t-s] b_{t-p}. So row a equals F_s(b) + sum_{t=1}^p a_t H_{t-s}(b), with s=|a|, H_u(b)=[|b|=u], F_s(b)=sum_{t=p+1}^n [|b|=t-s] b_{t-p}. Each row lies in V_s = span{F_s, H_{t-s}: 1<=t<=p}, dim <= p+1, and V_s depends only on s in {0..p}. So the row space lies in sum_{s=0}^p V_s, of dimension <= (p+1)^2. Consequence (conditional on H below): the natural order gives W_rank(HWB_n) <= (n+1)^2, so min over orders is <= (n+1)^2. H (CITED, NOT VERIFIED AT SOURCE; secondary arXiv 1912.01430 Prop. 4 proof attributes it to Bryant [10] with an improvement in Wegener's book Thm 4.10.2): every OBDD for HWB_n, for every variable order, has size >= 2^{n/5}. Then max level width >= (2^{n/5}-2)/(n+1), so W_OBDD(HWB_n) >= 2^{Omega(sqrt(W_rank))}, which refutes any polynomial bound W_OBDD <= poly(W_rank) on the HWB family, conditional on H. structure.lemma: Over any field F, for a 0/1 matrix M with N columns, r = rank_F(M) and D = number of distinct rows: r <= D <= 2^r. Consequently, for each variable order pi, W_rank(pi) <= W_OBDD(pi) <= 2^{W_rank(pi)}, where W_OBDD(pi) is the maximum over cuts of the number of distinct subfunctions and W_rank(pi) the maximum over cuts of rank_F of the cut matrix, and the same sandwich holds for min over pi.
structure.proved_step: Proof. Rows of M lie in V = rowspace_F(M), dim V = r. Distinct rows span V, so D >= r. Let B be an r x N matrix whose rows form a basis of V, and S a set of r columns with B_S invertible over F. For v = cB in V, v_S = c B_S, so v is determined by v_S; restriction to S is injective on V. Distinct 0/1 rows of M are distinct elements of V whose restrictions lie in {0,1}^S, a set of 2^r elements, so D <= 2^r. The order consequence follows by applying this to each cut, since distinct subfunctions at a cut equal distinct rows of its cut matrix.

If L and R are both the identity except R=diag(1,0), then both local factors are nonzero, the crossing-edge dimension product is 2, and rank(T)=1. More generally, rank(LR)≤2, with strict inequality whenever either factor is singular and LR is nonzero. Proof: contraction over the internal index is matrix multiplication. Its image lies in im(L), so rank(LR)≤rank(L)≤2; likewise rank(LR)≤rank(R). For the displayed choice LR=diag(1,0), whose rank is 1. Thus the edge-product bound is not in general an equality even for nonzero local factors and a nonzero represented tensor. This is a repair of the failed all-zero discovery search by excluding zero tensors and identifying a smallest explicit cancellation example.

structure.proved_step: statement: For L,R in K^{2×2} over any field K, rank(LR)=2 if and only if both L and R are invertible. Proof: If both are invertible, LR is invertible, hence has rank 2. Conversely, if rank(LR)=2, then rank(LR)≤rank(L) and rank(LR)≤rank(R), by image containment (and its transpose). Thus both factors have rank at least 2; since they are 2×2, both have rank 2 and are invertible.

structure.proved_step: statement: Let U,V,W be finite-dimensional vector spaces over a field K, and let B:U→V and A:V→W be linear maps. Then rank(A∘B)=rank(B) if and only if ker(A)∩im(B)={0}. Proof: Restrict A to im(B). Its kernel is exactly ker(A)∩im(B), and its image is A(im(B))=im(A∘B). By rank-nullity on this restriction, dim im(A∘B)=dim im(B)−dim(ker(A)∩im(B)). Since dim im(B)=rank(B), equality of the two ranks holds exactly when the intersection is zero. Thus a contraction loses rank precisely when the first map annihilates a nonzero direction that the second map can produce.

In particular, rank(T)=dim Z if and only if L is surjective and R is injective. Proof: The restriction R|_{im(L)} has image im(T) and kernel im(L)∩ker(R). Rank-nullity gives rank(T)=dim im(L)−dim(im(L)∩ker(R))=rank(L)−dim(...). Since rank(T)≤rank(L)≤dim Z, equality rank(T)=dim Z forces rank(L)=dim Z, so L is surjective; then the intersection condition forces ker(R)={0}, so R is injective. Conversely, if L is surjective and R injective, then R∘L has image R(Z), whose dimension is dim Z.

structure.lemma: CLAMPING LEMMA (self-made, bookkeeping level). Let B bound |W_{j,i}| and let rho fix the first l variables. The residual of bottom gate j is [W_rest . y >= s_j], where s_j = t_j - W_pre . rho. Since |W_rest . y| <= B(n-l), the residual is determined by clamp(s_j, -B(n-l), B(n-l)+1), so it has at most 2B(n-l)+2 values. The residual of f = C1 XOR C2 is a function of the vector of clamped shifts of the 2m bottom gates. Hence K_l <= min(2^l, (2Bn+2)^(2m)).

structure.lemma: REPAIR OF THE JOINT COUNT FOR CONSTANT q (partial; does NOT close G0001, G0002 or G0004). Let f = g_1 xor ... xor g_q over a fixed variable order, with g_i(x) = [W_i . x >= t_i] single threshold gates, and prefix length l, k = n - l. Then for every l: K_l(f) <= min(2^l, (2^k + 1)^q), and so sum_l K_l(f) <= (n+1) 2^{q(n+1)/(q+1)}.
structure.proved_step: PROOF. Fix a prefix a in {0,1}^l and write theta_i(a) = t_i - W_i1 . a. The residual of g_i is y -> [W_i2 . y >= theta_i(a)], which depends only on the cell of theta_i(a) among the sorted subset sums of W_i2 (at most 2^k values, hence at most 2^k + 1 cells). So the residual of f is determined by the tuple of q cell indices, giving at most (2^k+1)^q distinct residuals; trivially K_l <= 2^l. Since 2^k + 1 <= 2^{k+1}, min(2^l, 2^{q(n-l+1)}) is maximised when l = q(n+1-l), with value 2^{q(n+1)/(q+1)} (real maximum of min(l, q(n+1-l))). Summing over the n+1 levels gives the bound. CONSEQUENCE: for constant q, sum_l K_l <= (n+1) 2^{qn/(q+1) + O(1)} = 2^n / n^{omega(1)}, saving a factor 2^{-n/(q+1)}. For q = 2m with m bottom gates per circuit, the exponent q/(q+1) tends to 1 as m grows, so the bound becomes trivial at m = n^1.5 (this is the G0004 obstacle). Status: not source-checked, may already be known in the OBDD literature. Checked numerically in the next run.

structure.refuted_approach: CLAMPED-SHIFT COUNTING (R0884, exploratory). For a split at level l, let kappa_l(a) = clip(t_j - W1_j.a, lo_j, hi_j+1) over prefixes a in {0,1}^l, with lo_j, hi_j the min and max of W2_j.y over the suffix cube. Measured on random XOR-free THR o THR, m = round(n^1.5), weights in {-2..2}, thresholds in {-3..3}, 3 reps, n = 14 and 16 (cm-ee85f99d59a84796, cm-83e60a2450b14f79): D_clamp(l) = 2^l exactly for every l and every rep, so the clamped vectors are pairwise distinct on prefixes and the count gives no compression. The compression of K_l below 2^l (exact residual count, max over reps: n=14, l=9 gives 53 of 512; l=10 gives 41 of 1024; n=16, l=5 gives 1 of 32) comes from the top-level threshold, not from the bottom shift vectors. Consequence: any proof of G0001 must use the top-level threshold structure (the sum over gates with weights v_j) and cannot be a bound on the bottom shift vectors. The repair target becomes: a bound on the number of distinct values of the top sum over suffix cubes, uniform in the prefix.
